en: For a major exhibition titled

, held from September 2014 through March 2015 at the National Taiwan Museum in Taipei, a large billboard greeted visitors and passersby with four distinct examples of Taiwanese indigenous textile manufacture, of varied pattern and age, all dominated by the color red. Inside, displays of Atayal cloth occupied fully one-half of the palatial museum’s first floor. It was a complex installation: one-hundred-year-old, disembodied fabrics were juxtaposed with updated designs on sleek black mannequins; colonial-era ethnological surveys shared space with large color photos of contemporary weavers consulting them; and numerous imperial-era postcards illustrated the diversity, antiquity, and daily uses of the displayed fabrics.
zh: 2014年9月至2015年3月，台北国立台湾博物馆举办了一场题为《彩虹与蜻蜓》的展览（全名《彩虹与蜻蜓——泰雅服饰与排湾琉璃珠的对话特展》）。一块大广告牌以四件各具特色的台湾原住民纺织品迎接参观者与路人，它们纹样与年代各异，却都以红色为主调。馆内，泰雅族布料的陈列足足占据了这座宫殿般博物馆一楼的一半。这是一场多层次的陈列：百年前独立陈列的织物，与光滑黑色人体模型上的更新设计并置；殖民时期的民族学调查，与当代织工查阅这些调查的大幅彩色照片共处一室；众多帝国时期的明信片则展示了所陈列织物的不同种类、悠久历史与日常用途。

en: The Taiwan Government-General established the National Taiwan Museum in 1908, at the height of Japan’s camphor wars against the Atayal, Sediq, and Truku peoples who produced much of the cloth in this exhibition. The museum’s current structure was completed in 1915, the year Sakuma Samata left office and declared victory in the war against the northern tribes. As the scorched earth, free-fire zones, and land-dispossession policies of that era displayed the negative effects of sovereign power, the coterminous planning, construction, and stocking of the museum exemplified the positivities generated under TGG auspices in the colonial period.
zh: 台湾总督府于1908年设立国立台湾博物馆，其时正值日本对泰雅、赛德克与德路固诸族的樟脑战争高峰——这些族群生产了本次展览中的大部分布料。博物馆如今的建筑于1915年落成，正是佐久间左马太卸任、宣布对北部各部落的战争告捷的那一年。如果说那个时代的焦土、可不加辨别地开火的区域与土地剥夺政策展示了主权权力的负面效应，那么与之同时的博物馆的规划、建造与藏品征集，则体现了殖民时期在总督府主持下主权权力所产生的建构性成果。

en: The

exhibition, housed in a neoclassical, neocolonial edifice, was in good measure a dusting off, repackaging, and repurposing of the artifacts collected among indigenes during the Japanese occupation. Therefore, it revealed how colonial ethnography, museum practices, and photography were (and remain) active partners in the sustenance and revival of Atayal culture, which was also packaged in this exhibition as an element of Taiwan’s national heritage. The silhouette outline maps of Taiwan’s geobody that decorated the exhibition mark out Atayal and Paiwan homelands as the familiar second-order geobodies found on Inō’s 1900 map (see
illustrated the difficulty of imagining modern Taiwan without its indigenous complement or indigenous Taiwan without its modern complement.
zh: 《彩虹与蜻蜓》展览栖身于一座新古典主义、新殖民风格的大厦，在很大程度上是对日本占领期间从原住民中收集的文物的重新整理、包装和利用。因此，它揭示了殖民民族志、博物馆实践与摄影如何曾是（且至今仍是）泰雅文化维系与复兴的积极参与者——这种文化在本次展览中也被包装为台湾的国家文化遗产的一个要素。装饰展览的台湾地理体轮廓剪影地图，把泰雅与排湾的故土标划为伊能1900年地图上那种熟悉的二阶地理体（见
）。《彩虹与蜻蜓》表明：想象现代台湾若没有原住民这一组成部分，或原住民台湾若没有现代性这一组成部分，是何等困难。

en: This chapter recounts a 150-year history of indigenous-outsider transactions centered on red-dyed cloth. It explains how the oldest artifacts in the

exhibition conjoined global trade circuits, cross-cultural technological adaptations, colonial collecting, and Atayal social reproduction. In a word, this thread of colonial and postcolonial history illustrates how indigeneity and modernity coproduced each other.
zh: 本章讲述一段以染成红色的布匹为中心的、长达150年的原住民与外来者交易史。它解释《彩虹与蜻蜓》展览中最古老的文物如何把全球贸易网络、跨文化技术调适、殖民收藏与泰雅社会再生产结合到一起。一言以蔽之，这条殖民与后殖民历史的线索，说明了原住民性与现代性如何相互塑造。

en: GLOBAL ENTANGLEMENT AND LOCAL RESPONSES
zh: 全球纠缠与地方回应

en: U.S. consul to Taiwan James W. Davidson dated the “beginning of the commercial career of [Taiwan]... from 1858, when the two Hong Kong firms, Jardine Matheson & Co. and Dent & Co. first engaged the Formosan trade.” Between that year and 1865, British, Russian, French, and American diplomats signed treaties with the Qing to open Danshui, Tainan, Jilong, and Gaoxiong to foreign commerce.

The next decade saw a lucrative tea, camphor, and sugar export boom. Taiwanese merchants and laborers organized and directed most of the trade, while a few scattered Western missionaries, exporters, and a lone British consul constituted the meager foreign presence.

However, the frequent disappearance of mariners on and off the coast (see chapter 1) prompted a few foreign agents to leave the security of ports to ransom survivors or locate their remains. Others traversed the island out of curiosity, to find commercial opportunities, or to win souls for Christ.
zh: 美国驻台领事詹姆斯·W. 戴维森把“〔台湾〕商业生涯的开端……定在1858年，那一年怡和洋行与宝顺洋行这两家香港商行首次涉足福尔摩沙贸易。”从那年到1865年，英、俄、法、美外交官与清朝签约，开放淡水、台南、基隆、高雄对外贸易。
接下来十年出现了利润丰厚的茶叶、樟脑与糖出口繁荣。台湾商人与劳工组织并主导了大部分贸易，而零星散布的西方传教士、出口商与一名英国领事，外籍人士寥寥无几。
然而，船员在台湾沿岸和近海频繁失踪（见第1章），促使一些外国代理人离开港口的安全地带，去赎回幸存者或寻找他们的遗骸。另一些人则出于好奇、为寻找商机、或劝人皈依基督教而穿越全岛。

en: The guarantees of safety to foreigners spelled out in the Treaty of Tianjin of 1858, however, were moot in interior destinations beyond the limits of Qing administrative control. For such journeys, local trading-post operators and subofficials known as

(interpreters) outfitted visitors with provisions, advice, and guides. Among the most noted items of purchase were gifts for indigenous hosts. U.S. consul to Xiamen Charles LeGendre’s 1869 meeting with the Tuilasok chief Toketok (nudged to fruition with a baggage train of gifts) and Captain Douglas Cassel’s 1874 meeting with Sabaree chief Isa (also concluded with lavish displays of generosity) are two prominent examples of the importance of gifts for borderland diplomacy (see chapter 1). So too with the aforementioned treks by Ueno Sen’ichi, Hashiguchi Bunzō, Kawano Shuichirō, and other Japanese emissaries to the “savage territory” in the 1890s. Gifts performed multiple functions in these settings. They were initially a means of paying for services rendered or expectations of future assistance, to be sure. But they were much more.
zh: 然而，1858年《天津条约》中明文规定的外国人安全保障，在清朝行政控制范围之外的内陆地区却无法落实。对于这类旅程，当地贸易站经营者与称为通事（tongshi，即译员）的佐杂官，给来访者提供给养、建议和向导。最常购买的物品中，就有给原住民主人的礼物。美国驻厦门领事李仙得1869年与猪朥束头目卓杞笃的会面（靠一支运送礼物的队伍促成），以及道格拉斯·卡塞尔上尉1874年与射麻里头目伊萨的会面（同样以大量赠礼促成），是礼物对边疆外交至关重要的两个突出例子（见第1章）。1890年代上野专一、桥口文藏、河野主一郎及其他日本使者前往“蕃地”的上述跋涉也是如此。在这些场合，礼物履行多重功能。诚然，它们起初是酬谢已经获得或预期日后获得的协助的手段。但它们远不止于此。

en: Presentations of gifts were also occasions for recording the emotional states of recipients and gauging the dispositions of little-known peoples as either “greedy,” “honest,” or “uncorrupted.” Gifts also fostered trade dependency among indigenes. The regulation of gift giving was also implemented to reform mores, punish misdeeds, and incentivize compliance. Finally, gifts were recycled and repurposed. Manufactured containers were brought back to villages for reuse, while red-dyed textiles were disassembled and reassembled into traditional cloth and clothing, to be reexported to anthropologists, curators, and tourists as cultural items. As commodities in the Japanese curio, art, and souvenir markets, or as objects of aesthetic or scholarly contemplation, the reexported cloth and clothing became touchstones for metropolitan discourses on progress, primitivism, and cultural relativism. As such, these objects took their place next to the Gwanghwamun Gate in Seoul, Korean celadon wares, or bamboo and wickerwork from Taiwan.
zh: 赠送礼物也是记录受赠者情绪状态、把鲜为人知人群的性情判定为“贪婪”“诚实”或“未经世俗沾染”的场合。礼物还在原住民中培育贸易依赖。对赠礼的规管也被用来改良风俗、惩罚恶行、激励顺从。最后，礼物被回收与重新利用。制成品容器被带回村里重复使用，而染红纺织品则被拆解、重组为传统布料与服装，再作为文化物品重新出口给人类学家、策展人与游客。作为日本古玩、艺术与纪念品市场上的商品，或作为审美与学术沉思的对象，这些再出口的布料与服装成了日本本土讨论进步、原始主义和文化相对主义时的参照物。如此，这些物件便与首尔的光化门、朝鲜青瓷，或台湾的竹器藤编并列。

en: In a famous consular report that recounted his 1869 encounter with Toketok, Charles LeGendre wrote:
zh: 在一份记述他1869年与卓杞笃相遇的著名领事报告中，李仙得写道：

en: I gave the chief one hundred and eighty yards of red camlet, a small pistol, a single-barrel shot gun (unserviceable), and a spear... an ivory spy-glass and case... some beads, and a quantity of rings, bracelets, and a case of gin...

children: Toketok had not expected this attention, and he was evidently much touched by it. “If you have brought all this to buy me,” said he, “you have taken a useless care, for you had my word; but if you hand me these presents as a token of friendship, I receive them with pleasure

zh: 我给了头目一百八十码红色羽纱（camlet）、一支小手枪、一支单管猎枪（已不堪使用）、一柄矛……一具象牙望远镜连同镜盒……一些珠子，还有大量戒指、手镯，以及一箱杜松子酒……卓杞笃没料到会受到如此礼遇，显然深受感动。“如果你带这一切来收买我，”他说，“那你白费了心思，因为你早已得到我的承诺；但如果你把这些礼物作为友谊的表示交给我，我欣然收下。”

en: Toketok’s reported speech, to the effect that the 180 yards of red camlet and other gifts were mere “tokens of friendship” and that LeGendre had “taken a useless care,” is significant for reprising assertions that indigenes were disinterested in material gain or profit. Toketok’s soliloquy, recorded after the fact and at the end of a translation relay from Paiwan to Minnan Chinese to English, does not jibe with less florid descriptions of similar transactions. Other travelers to Taiwan recorded Toketok’s businesslike collection of cash fees for the upkeep of stranded sailors.

LeGendre himself remarked in unpublished writings that Toketok’s leadership of the eighteen tribes was financially draining and that the leader was known to drive hard bargains for ransoms of foreigners.
Douglas Fix has argued that when LeGendre arrived in Langqiao in 1867, Toketok’s influence was at an apogee. By 1869, his hold on power had become precarious, in part for lack of funds.
But if LeGendre’s imputation of native simplicity to a master negotiator rings false, it was not exceptional.
zh: 据转述，卓杞笃的话大意是：那180码红羽纱与其他礼物不过是“友谊的表示”，李仙得“白费了心思”。这番转述值得注意，因为它再次呈现了原住民无意追求物质利益或利润的说法。卓杞笃的独白是事后记录的，而且从排湾语经闽南语转译为英语，与对类似交易较为平实的记载并不吻合。其他到台湾的旅行者记录了卓杞笃对遇险船员的食宿按价收取现金。
李仙得自己在未刊文稿中说，卓杞笃维持十八社联盟的领导地位耗资不菲，而这位首领在谈外国人的赎金时出了名地寸步不让。
道格拉斯·菲克斯论证说，1867年李仙得抵达琅峤时，卓杞笃的影响力如日中天。到1869年，他对权力的掌控已岌岌可危，部分原因是缺钱。
李仙得笔下这位谈判高手被写成了一个淳朴的原住民。这样的描述虽难以取信，当时却相当常见。

en: Edward House, a journalist who accompanied the Japanese invasion in 1874 and championed all of LeGendre’s political positions, made similar observations. House had occasion to witness coastal Han Taiwanese bargain with troops for land, provisions, and wages as the army built its first camp, while House also reported on Japanese conferences with the Tuilasok and Sabaree leaders to negotiate alliances, passage, and land for an east coast garrison. At a June 8 meeting, House wrote of Paiwan emissaries that “hints of the presents that were awaiting them at head-quarters did not affect their resolution, and it seemed impossible to move them, when suddenly Isa, stirred by what impulse I cannot imagine, unless it may have been the recollection of having made a promise at the time of his last visit, announced that he would go.”
zh: 爱德华·豪斯——一名随1874年日本入侵而来、拥护李仙得全部政治立场的记者——作了类似观察。豪斯有机会目睹沿海台湾汉人在军队搭建第一座营地时，与部队就土地、给养与工资讨价还价；他也报道了日本人与猪朥束、射麻里首领的会谈，商谈联盟、通行，以及东海岸驻军的用地。在6月8日的一次会面中，豪斯写到排湾使者：“暗示司令部有礼物等着他们，并未动摇他们的决心，似乎根本无法打动他们；忽然间，伊萨不知被什么冲动所驱使——我想象不出，除非是想起上次来访时作过的承诺——宣布他愿意去。”

en: For House, as for LeGendre, indigenes were indifferent to gifts but anxious to honor commitments. When Isa and a group of his confederate Paiwan headmen ceded a plot of land on the east coast for Japanese occupation, House wrote that offers “of payment were made, but the chiefs declined compensation, with the carelessness to gain which I have spoken of as characteristic of them.”

House drove home his larger point with a comparison: “The savages [House’s term for the Paiwanese] have nothing whatever of the Chinaman in their exterior aspect, and their ways of life are totally separate. The divergence of their disposition is most strikingly shown in the contrast between the insatiate greed of the West Coast [Han] and the indifference to gain of the mountaineers.”
zh: 对豪斯而言，正如对李仙得而言，原住民对礼物无动于衷，却急于履行承诺。当伊萨与一群结盟的排湾头目割让东海岸一块土地供日本占领时，豪斯写道，有人提出“付款，但头目们拒绝了补偿，带着我说过的那种他们特有的、对获利的淡漠。”
豪斯用一个对比进一步申明自己的论点：“野蛮人〔豪斯对排湾人的称呼〕在外表上丝毫没有支那人的影子，他们的生活方式也全然不同。他们性情上的差异，最鲜明地体现在西海岸〔汉人〕贪得无厌与山地人对利益漠然之间的对照中。”

en: LeGendre himself had several occasions to express vitriolic attitudes toward assorted Chinese officials and interpreters for their bad faith and greed, presaging Japanese scorn for Han Taiwanese who purportedly cheated indigenes in the so-called “border trade.” In detailed reports of individual encounters, however, we find that the stark line House and others drew between the “Chinaman” and the “mountaineer” did not hold, calling into question their judgments that Han and indigenous attitudes toward profit or material gain were antithetical. For example, Toketok—the quintessential noble savage in the passage quoted above—himself slept in a Chinese bed, while one of his brothers could read and write Chinese. Isa, his successor as the dominant political figure in lower Hengchun, understood spoken Chinese. The “half-caste” allies and hirelings whom LeGendre and House distanced from China for having lived beyond the reach of Qing territory were referred to as “Chinese” by Douglas Cassel in unpublished correspondence—a contradiction that the American consul adjusted with a heavy editorial hand.
zh: 李仙得本人也曾多次痛斥各色清朝官员和通事背信贪婪，预示了日本人对据称在所谓“边界贸易”中欺骗原住民的台湾汉人的蔑视。然而，在对单次相遇的详细报告中，我们发现豪斯等人在“支那人”与“山地人”之间划下的鲜明界线并不成立，这就使人质疑他们关于汉人与原住民对利润或物质利益态度截然对立的判断。例如，卓杞笃——上文引段中典型的高贵野蛮人——自己睡的是中式床，而他的一个兄弟能读写汉文。伊萨，即接替他成为恒春南部主导政治人物的人，听得懂汉语口语。李仙得与豪斯因为那些“混血”盟友与雇工居于清朝控制范围之外，便不把他们归作中国人，道格拉斯·卡塞尔却在未刊通信中称他们为“中国人”——这一矛盾，被这位美国领事以大刀阔斧的编辑手法抹平了。

en: In the long run, as this chapter shall argue, the triad of reinforcing stereotypes—impartial Japanese, avaricious Chinese, and innocent indigenes—became a self-fulfilling prophecy, as Japanese policies grounded in this discourse would eventually isolate Atayal, Sediq, Truku, Bunun, and Paiwanese from the market economy.

To be sure, the economies of upland rural Taiwan were not nearly as monetized or commoditized as the Han-dominated lowlands when Japanese colonists arrived in 1895. Therefore, a different sensibility and approach to commerce, gain, and valuation plausibly obtained in and beyond the savage border of Taiwan. At the same time, since this stereotype was resistant to empirical disconfirmation and durable in the face of historical change, it also functioned as a racial attribute, fixing certain populations with particular immutable characteristics in the discourses and legal apparatus of the colonizing power.
zh: 从长远看，正如本章将要论证的，这组三种相互强化的刻板印象——公正的日本人、贪婪的中国人、天真无邪的原住民——成了自我实现的预言，因为植根于这套话语的日本政策，最终把泰雅、赛德克、德路固、布农与排湾人隔离于市场经济之外。
诚然，1895年日本殖民者到来时，台湾山地乡村经济的货币化与商品化程度，远不及汉人主导的低地。因此，在台湾“生番界”及其以外，商贸观念、获利方式和价值衡量很可能与低地有别。与此同时，由于这一刻板印象没有被相反的事实推翻，也经受住了历史变迁，它也充当了一种种族属性，在殖民强权的话语与法律装置中，把某些人群固定为具有特定不可变特征的存在。

en: Like other travelers during the treaty-port period, LeGendre had an ax to grind with the local Qing officials, who seemed to thwart his every initiative, and Hakka intermediaries who profited from their monopoly on access to interior settlements. The everyday forms of resistance LeGendre faced are unsurprising, since his ability to travel to the interior of Taiwan was a direct result of the success of British arms in mainland China. Traders and diplomats in post-1842 Chinese treaty ports, LeGendre prominent among them, discovered that the stroke of a pen in Tianjin or Beijing did not magically transform Taiwan into a welcoming site for foreign residence or an arena of untrammeled access.
zh: 与通商口岸时期的其他旅行者一样，李仙得对当地清朝官员心存不满——他们似乎阻挠他的每一项倡议——也对那些靠垄断进入内陆聚落的通道而牟利的客家中介不满。李仙得遭遇的日常抵抗形式并不令人意外，因为他能到台湾内陆旅行，正是英国武力在中国大陆得逞的直接结果。1842年后中国通商口岸的商人与外交官——李仙得是其中显眼的一员——发现，仅凭在天津或北京签署条约，并不能让台湾马上欢迎外国人居住或任其自由出入。

en: There is probably more than a kernel of truth to the perception that indigenes were more open to negotiation with foreigners than Han Taiwanese, since they sought allies in struggles against settlers or Qing officials over resources and territory. That is to say, the “greedy Chinese, innocent indigene” trope may have fairly reflected the experiences of individual diarists. There is also the possibility that Toketok’s attitude toward gifts was context specific, dynamic, and grounded in a cosmology more intricate and meaningful than the sort of crass considerations that suggest themselves in LeGendre’s and House’s accounts. Anthropologist Kamimura Tōru has suggested as much by reconstructing a network of Parijarijao (“Paiwanized” Puyuma) chiefs and big men that was connected by patterned exchanges resembling a kula ring.
zh: 认为原住民比台湾汉人更乐于与外国人谈判，这一看法恐怕不止有一点真实，因为他们在与移民或清朝官员争夺资源与领土的斗争中寻求盟友。也就是说，“贪婪的中国人、天真无邪的原住民”这一套话，可能相当忠实地反映了个别旅行记录的作者的经验。还有一种可能：卓杞笃对礼物的态度是随情境变化的，植根于一种宇宙观，它比李仙得与豪斯记述中浮现的那种粗鄙考量更复杂、更有意义。人类学家纸村彻通过重构一个帕里贾里焦（Parijarijao，“排湾化”的卑南）头目与大人物（big men）的网络，暗示了这一点；该网络由类似库拉圈（kula ring）的模式化交换连接起来。

en: In Kamimura’s view, the Langqiao Peninsula’s indigenous Skaro lineages, with Tuilasok’s Toketok first among them as the big stride chief (ōmata tōmoku), ritually subordinated common Paiwan village chiefs (such as the Mudan headman, for example) through gifting relations. These transactions resembled tributary relations in some regards—as they featured hierarchical yet reciprocal ritual exchange—while they partook in some aspects of a kula ring, insofar as hierarchies were ratified only when equilibrium was restored at the termination of a cycle of gifting and countergifting. In Kamimura’s reconstruction, Toketok, as the big stride chief, and Isa and the secondary great chief (futamata tōmoku) traveled widely to seasonal festivals to present finished goods such cloth, ritual daggers, alcohol, and millet cakes “downward.” In return, subordinate chiefs, themselves members of aristocratic Paiwan lineages, countergifted “upward” with domesticated and hunted meat and presentations of large quantities of alcohol at banquets. When LeGendre and his men showed up with a large cargo of finished goods, which he lavished upon Toketok in exchange for alcoholic beverages and roast meat, Toketok situated LeGendre, quite publicly, in the position of one to whom fealty is rendered in return for protection, thereby inverting the ōmata tōmoku’s place in the gifting cycle—he became a receiver of finished goods instead of a supplier. If such were the case, then Toketok’s hesitation to receive gifts can be interpreted as appropriate behavior for an ōmata tōmoku in a ritual gifting context. Kamimura regards the instances of Toketok’s more avaricious bargaining as “enclave” transactions conducted outside the sphere of ritual relations and networks.
zh: 在纸村看来，琅峤半岛的原住民斯卡罗宗族——其中以担任大股头目（ōmata tōmoku）的猪朥束首领卓杞笃为首——通过赠礼关系，在仪式上使普通排湾村社头目（例如牡丹头目）处于从属地位。这些交易在某些方面类似朝贡关系——因为它们具有等级性却又互惠的仪式交换——同时在某些方面又带有库拉圈的特征，因为只有在赠礼与回礼的一个周期终结、均衡恢复时，等级才得到认可。按纸村的重构，卓杞笃作为大股头目，与伊萨及二股头目（futamata tōmoku）到各地参加季节性庆典，把布料、仪式匕首、酒、粟米糕等制成品“向下”赠送。作为回报，从属头目——他们本身也是排湾贵族宗族的成员——用饲养家畜或狩猎所得的肉“向上”回礼，并在宴会上奉送大量酒。当李仙得一行人带着大批制成品出现、慷慨赠予卓杞笃以换取酒类与烤肉时，卓杞笃相当公开地把李仙得置于这样一个位置：向对方效忠的人可得到他的保护。这样一来，大股头目在赠礼循环中的位置便颠倒了：他成了制成品的接受者，而非供应者。若果真如此，那么卓杞笃对接受礼物的犹豫，就可以解读为大股头目在仪式赠礼情境中的恰当行为。纸村把卓杞笃那些较为计较利益的讨价还价，视为在仪式关系与网络之外进行的“飞地”交易。

en: Paiwan and Puyuma chiefly genealogies, foundation myths, and the specifics of prestations at festivals were not recorded until after the Japanese arrived as a colonizing power in 1895. Therefore, this more nuanced view of indigenous dispositions to gifts was not available to LeGendre, House, Mizuno, Kabayama, and the other men who became Toketok’s and Isa’s unwitting amanuenses. In the absence of countervailing explanatory frameworks, their treaty-port era jottings were elevated from commercial intelligence reports to sociological verities. For one, the musings of LeGendre and House, a U.S. consul and a journalist for the

, respectively, were widely disseminated and archived for posterity in libraries and repositories. In addition, and more importantly, hundreds of LeGendre’s reports, missives, and memoranda were translated into Japanese and read by Japanese officials. Ueno Sen’ichi, an assiduous consumer and translator of treaty-port documents, elaborated upon LeGendre’s discourse in his seminal official writings in the 1890s, while Mizuno Jun himself echoed similar sentiments. Mizuno’s early pronouncements as Taiwan’s highest ranking civil official in 1895 cemented the “greedy Chinese, innocent indigene” binary in TGG circulars and archived reports.
zh: 排湾与卑南的头目世系、起源神话，以及节庆馈赠的细节，直到1895年日本作为殖民强权到来之后才被记录。因此，这种对原住民如何看待赠礼的这种更细致的理解，李仙得、豪斯、水野、桦山，以及其他成为卓杞笃与伊萨不自觉记录者的人，是无从获得的。在缺乏可反驳这些推论的解释框架的情况下，他们通商口岸时代的随笔，从商业情报报告被抬升为社会学真理。其一，李仙得与豪斯——分别是美国领事与《纽约邮报》记者——的观察被广泛传播，并为后世存档于图书馆与典藏库。此外，更重要的是，李仙得数百份报告、书信与备忘录被译成日文，供日本官员阅读。上野专一作为潜心研读并翻译通商口岸文献的人，在1890年代其开创性的官方著作中阐发了李仙得的话语，而水野遵本人也呼应了类似看法。水野1895年作为台湾最高级文官时所作的早期表态，把“贪婪的中国人、天真无邪的原住民”这一二元对立固化进了总督府的通令与存档报告。

en: As a permutation of the above-mentioned treaty-port era discourse, the trope of the “innocent” indigene took on new valences in colonial Taiwan. The Qing dynasty and its corrupt mandarinate were no longer relevant. The new foils were the untrustworthy bicultural border denizens discussed in chapter 2, the “interpreters” (
). This substitution of

for mandarins mirrored the configuration of northern Taiwan’s camphor forests as another “closed country” to be opened as an arena for high-velocity capitalism. Partly because they contained forests that sustained populations of animals, sources of clean water, fish, vegetables, and other resources, indigenes defended these lands with alacrity.
zh: 作为上述通商口岸时代话语的一个变体，“天真无邪”的原住民这一套话在殖民台湾获得了新的意涵。清朝及其腐败的官僚集团已不再相干。新的对照物，是第2章讨论的那些被视为不可靠、同时通晓两种文化的边疆居民——“通事”（tongshi）。通事取代清朝官员成了被指摘的对象。这一转变映照出，北台湾的樟脑林被当作另一个有待打开的“锁国”，资本主义可由此迅速扩张。部分因为这些森林出产或维系着野生动物、清洁水源、鱼类、可食植物等资源，原住民因而积极保卫这些土地。

en: Nonetheless, the contest here was not between proto-environmental subsistence producers and rapacious capitalist invaders. Rather, the savage territory was an active zone of ongoing economic exploitation, like Chinese ports before the arrival of Western gunboat diplomacy. As Takeshi Hamashita has written of this maritime economy, the new entrants—this time the Japanese—did not displace an isolated traditional economy with profit-driven, translocal commercial activity. Instead, they overlaid a new system of rules and procedures and connected an existing system to wider currents of global trade. In this milieu, aptly described by Antonio Tavares as a late-imperial exchange economy, indigenes, Han Taiwanese, and operators who straddled both groups exploited these forests for commodities, not just birds, deer, firewood, and mushrooms.
zh: 然而，这里的较量并非发生在具有早期环保意识、以生产维生的人与贪婪的资本主义入侵者之间。相反，蕃地是一个持续经济开发的活跃地带，就像西方炮舰外交到来之前的中国港口。正如滨下武志论及这一海洋经济时所写，新进入者——这次是日本人——并没有用利润驱动的跨地域商业活动取代一个孤立的传统经济。相反，他们叠加了一套新的规则与程序，把一个既有体系连接到全球贸易更广泛的潮流中。在这一被安东尼奥·塔瓦雷斯恰切地描述为晚期帝国交换经济的环境里，原住民、台湾汉人，以及横跨两个群体的经营者都已在开发这些森林。除了猎鸟捕鹿、采柴摘菇，他们还从中获取供交易的商品。

en: As the Taiwan Government-General turned its attention to camphor as a fiscal boon for its ailing balance sheet, Japanese attributions of greed and faithlessness to

(interpreters) reflected frustration with “toll states” that earned money by taxing and monopolizing access to camphor producers. For actuarially minded administrators in Taipei and Tokyo, this intermediary layer of brokers presented an obstacle to the efficient extraction of high volumes of product.

The trope of Chinese greed and indigenous honesty also justified colonial rule. As Japanese displaced interpreters, private militias, and Qing armies as agents of dispossession, the insistence upon indigenous innocence and victimhood validated Japanese policies to annex land, engage in forced relocation, and restrict Han immigration. Because indigenes did not understand the concept of private property, ran the argument, they could not make legal claims to title deeds for land. Consequently, their legalistic transformation into economic wards of the state allowed the government-general to sell off “excess land” to logging companies, in a repeat of the gambit used in Hokkaidō vis-à-vis Ainu peoples in 1899.
zh: 当台湾总督府把目光转向樟脑、视其为改善财政困境的进项时，日本人把贪婪与背信归于通事，反映了对那些靠征税并垄断交易者接触樟脑生产者的渠道来牟利的“关卡型政体”的挫败感。对台北与东京那些精算思维的行政官而言，这一层居间商妨碍了当局高效、大量地取得樟脑。

中国人贪婪、原住民诚实的套话也为殖民统治提供了正当性。当日本人取代通事、私人武装与清军，成为剥夺的代理人时，将原住民认定为无辜的受害者，给日本侵占土地、强制迁移及限制汉人移民的政策提供了正当性。论证说，因为原住民不懂私有财产概念，他们便没有资格依法主张土地所有权。这样一来，原住民在法律上成了经济事务由国家监护的人。这使总督府得以把“多余土地”变卖给伐木公司——重演了1899年在北海道对阿伊努人使用的策略。

en: Like any other colonial project, however, Japanese rule contained its own internal tensions, while it underwent historical vicissitudes. A competing discourse generated by these same cross-border exchanges identified

red-striped capes as an element of a distinctive cultural ensemble. From the viewpoint of colonial ethnology, any cloth, implement, word list, or social convention that attached to “Atayalness” possessed a measure of intrinsic worth. As Scott Simon has noted, the ethnonym Atayal is a Japanese-era creation. Today, this imposed category has become an object of heated political contestation in the postcolonial period.

On the other hand, its origins were far from nefarious. The Japanese man who put the word Atayal into play recorded it as an autonym, a term provided to him in collaboration with agentive Atayal peoples.
zh: 然而，与任何其他殖民工程一样，日本统治包含自身的内部张力，并经历历史变迁。由这些同样的跨境交换生成的一种竞争性话语，把泰雅红条纹披风认定为一整套独特文化的组成部分。从殖民民族学的视角看，任何与“泰雅性”有关的布料、器具、词汇表或社会习俗，都拥有某种内在价值。正如斯科特·西蒙所指出的，族名“泰雅”是日殖时期的创造。今天，这一强加的类别在后殖民时期已成为激烈政治争夺的对象。
另一方面，当初提出这一名称的人并无这种恶意。最早让“泰雅”一词通行起来的日本人是在与泰雅人合作时，记下他们主动提供的这一自称。

en: In fact, the term

had its origins in a dissenting discourse. Yamaji Katsuhiko’s study of the centrality of Atayal textiles and Paiwan woodcarving to Japanese-indigenous relations over the past century is important in this regard. Echoing the findings of Hu Chia-yu, Yamaji notes that early Japanese descriptions of Atayal cloth juxtaposed them with other elements of ethnic identity—face tattoos, housing architecture, origin myths, and so on—to construct Atayal people as an ethnos. Hu’s translation from Inō’s famous 1900 survey is instructive: “The less abstract the costume design becomes, the higher its intellectual level tends to be. The more concrete [a] costume decoration becomes, the higher its intellectual level.... Thus, the weaving patterns of the Atayal costumes consist of straight lines and angles and elements arranged without clear order..., which reflect a lower intellectual level. The embroidery designs on the Paiwan costumes consist of pictorial animal figures... which demonstrates a higher intellectual level.”
zh: 事实上，“泰雅”一词起源于一种异议话语。山路胜彦关于过去一个世纪泰雅纺织品与排湾木雕在日本—原住民关系中居于中心地位的研究，在这方面很重要。呼应胡家瑜的发现，山路指出，早期日本人对泰雅布料的描述，把它们与族群身份的其他要素——纹面、房屋建筑、起源神话等等——并置，以把泰雅人建构为一个有共同文化特征的族群。胡家瑜对伊能著名的1900年调查的译文很有启发：“服装设计越不抽象，其智力水平往往越高。服装装饰越具体，其智力水平越高……因此，泰雅服装的织纹由直线、角以及排列无明显秩序的要素构成……反映较低的智力水平。排湾服装的刺绣图案由具象的动物图案构成……表明较高的智力水平。”

en: By the 1920s, however, such antiseptic (and at times derogatory) descriptions gave way to aesthetic engagement and emotional investment. As was the case with Paiwan wood carvings, Bunun song, and Amis dance, Atayal weaving provided Japanese academics, tourists, and impresarios with a means to rejuvenate a Japanese self ravaged by the atomism and dislocations of urbanized modernity.
zh: 然而到1920年代，这类冷冰冰（且时而贬损）的描述，让位于审美投入与情感投注。正如排湾木雕、布农歌谣与阿美舞蹈一样，泰雅织布为日本学者、游客与文化推手提供了一种手段，去恢复那个被现代都市生活中的个人孤立与社会脱节所损伤的日本人自我认同的活力。

en: Haruyama Meitetsu has argued that the colonial history of Taiwan cannot be written in isolation from political developments in Tokyo. For Haruyama, the twists and turns in the history of Taiwan’s administration were intimately linked to regime turnover in Japan’s central government. Haruyama rightly insists that Japan’s ruling elites were a dynamic and internally divided group and that one must specify “who, what, and where” when imputing motives and causality to “the metropole” in the study of colonial Taiwan.
The same can be said for Japanese consumer, artistic, and literary tastes. They too were various and protean, and they constituted a dynamic aspect of Taiwan’s history, as well.
zh: 春山明哲论证说，台湾的殖民史不能脱离东京的政治发展来书写。对春山而言，台湾施政史上的曲折，与日本中央政府的政权更迭紧密相连。春山正确地坚持，日本统治精英是一个动态、内部分裂的群体，研究殖民台湾时，如果把动机或原因归于“宗主国”，就必须具体交代涉及何人、何事、何地。
日本的消费、艺术与文学品味亦然。它们同样多样而多变，也构成了台湾历史的一个动态面向。

en: In his 1991 book

, Nicholas Thomas devised a useful framework for elucidating the long-term imbrication of indigenous renaissance with colonialism and its legacies, and for bringing translocal networks and economies to bear on the siloed studies of nationalist history or community-based ethnography. In his study of asymmetrical historical interactions between British imperial agents and Fiji and Samoan Islanders, Thomas proposes the “entanglement” metaphor as an alternative to “incorporation” (a triumphalist or extinction narrative of global capitalism’s rise to dominance) or “comparison” (the critique or lionization of capitalism through comparison with putatively alternative economic logics). The “entangled objects” model, which I employ in this analysis, steers a course between ascertaining the rate and extent of the periphery’s transformation by the core (“incorporation”) and the meticulous reconstruction of internally coherent ideal-typical systems of meaning (“comparison”).

The former method is that criticized by Haruyama as too deterministic and reliant on Marxist stage theories, while the latter approach comes from the efforts to write “internal” histories of indigenous peoples that filter out “external” influences.
zh: 尼古拉斯·托马斯在其1991年的著作《纠缠之物》中，设计了一个有用的框架，用以阐明原住民复兴与殖民主义及其遗产的长期交织，并把跨地域的经济活动及其网络引入民族主义史学或社区本位民族志那些孤立的研究。在他关于英国帝国代理人与斐济、萨摩亚岛民之间不对称历史互动的研究中，托马斯提出“纠缠”隐喻，作为“纳入”（一种关于全球资本主义崛起主导的凯旋主义或灭绝叙事）或“比较”（通过与据称另类的经济逻辑相比较来批判或颂扬资本主义）之外的替代。“纠缠之物”模型——我在本分析中采用的——同时避开两种方法的局限。一是侧重衡量边缘被核心改造的速率与程度（“纳入”），二是细致重构内部自洽的理想型意义体系（“比较”）。
前一种方法正是春山所批评的、过于决定论且依赖马克思主义阶段论的方法；后一种取径则来自书写原住民“内部”史、滤除“外部”影响的努力。

en: To illustrate, from an “incorporation” perspective, LeGendre’s presentation of the red cloth to Toketok is salient because it facilitated an agreement between a U.S. emissary and a powerful chieftain. The arrangement was but one in a series of ad hoc accords whose breakdown fomented the Japanese invasion of Taiwan in May 1874. As a result of this invasion, the Qing initiated more aggressive policies against indigenes from 1875 through 1895, further eroding their autonomy. Shortly thereafter, mechanized Japanese military might brought indigenous populations to heel beginning in 1903. By 1915 or so, Japan delivered the coup de grâce to indigenous sovereignty, ushering in an era of subordinate existence in the global division of labor and the colonial racial pecking order. In this rendering, 180 yards of red camlet is fungible—any gift might have served the same function. This conclusion is at odds with the inordinate attention paid to the specific contours of materiality by contemporary observers. Moreover, as an extinction narrative, the “incorporation model” does little to help us understand current developments in indigenous peoples’ rights recovery and renaissance or the continued attractions of primitivist consumerism.
zh: 举例来说，从“纳入”视角看，李仙得把红布赠予卓杞笃之所以重要，是因为它促成了一位美国使者与一位强势头目之间的协议。这一安排不过是一系列权宜协议中的一环，而这些协议的破裂促成了1874年5月日本对台湾的入侵。作为这次入侵的结果，清朝从1875年到1895年对原住民发起了更激进的政策，进一步侵蚀了他们的自治。此后不久，机械化的日本军事威力从1903年起开始制服原住民人群。到1915年前后，日本给了原住民主权致命一击，开启了一个在全球劳动分工与殖民种族等级秩序中从属存在的时代。在这一叙述中，180码红羽纱是可替代的——任何礼物都可能起到同样作用。这一结论与当时的观察者格外关注这件礼物的具体材质和特性的事实不符。此外，作为一种灭绝叙事，“纳入模型”几乎无助于我们理解当前原住民权利恢复与复兴的发展，或原始主义取向的消费何以经久不衰。

en: Using the comparative method would lead us in a different direction, and it also raises problems. Based on the voluminous travel reports and diplomatic correspondence available for southern Taiwan and anthropological fieldwork studies of Paiwanese kinship, political structure, and ideology, one could ascertain the role of red camlet in the redistributive political economy of the Eighteen-Tribe Confederation. Using models constructed by political anthropologists of Polynesia, one could then hypothesize to what extent Toketok was a chief or a big man, or try to figure out how his brushes with the global economy transformed his leadership style from one type to the other.
zh: 使用比较法则会把我们引向不同方向，它也有其局限。基于南台湾可得的大量旅行报告与外交通信，以及对排湾人亲属制度、政治结构与意识形态的人类学田野研究，人们可以确定红羽纱在十八社联盟再分配政治经济中的角色。借助波利尼西亚政治人类学家构建的模型，人们进而可以假设卓杞笃在在多大程度上属于头目或大人物这两种类型，或试图弄清他与全球经济的接触如何把他的领导风格从一种类型转变为另一种。

en: Having established the internal logic of Langqiao’s political economy and the meaning of gifts within it, one could then contrast it with the logic of monopoly capitalism and national sovereignty to identify what is distinctive, autochthonous, and original about Paiwanese social organization.

Like incorporation analyses, comparativist studies yield important insights. But as Thomas notes, the methodological insistence upon “difference” in comparative work has a tendency to consign actors in these systems to parallel, containerized temporalities, an analytical fiction that is belied by the phenomenon of meaningful cross-cultural exchange.
zh: 在确立了琅峤政治经济的内部逻辑及礼物在其中的意义之后，人们便可以把它与垄断资本主义和国家主权的逻辑相对照，以识别排湾社会组织中独特、土生土长、原初的东西。
与纳入分析一样，比较研究也产生重要洞见。但正如托马斯所指出的，比较工作在方法论上对“差异”的坚持，倾向于把这些体系中的行动者归入各自封闭、平行发展的历史时间——而有实际意义的跨文化交换恰好表明，这是一种虚构。

en: An “entangled objects” analysis instead lingers a bit longer on the materiality of LeGendre’s gift to take notice of the fact that indigenes refashioned imported red cloth to create what has come to be known as Atayal traditional clothing (see
). Illustrations and Japanese ethnological displays (see
) helped stabilize this marker of Atayal tradition.

）。插图与日本民族学展示（见
）使这一标志逐渐固定为泰雅传统的代表。

en: These garments in turn took on a variety of local meanings, values, and usages that had little relevance to the story of international relations but were, nonetheless, crucial for social reproduction in indigenous societies.

Following LeGendre’s red camlet through another iteration, we observe that the articles that have come to be known as traditional Atayal cloth were in turn reappropriated by Japanese of various stripes for a multitude of purposes during the colonial period (and beyond). As museum pieces, objects of study, and popular items at souvenir stands, Atayal textiles came to symbolize either a particular ethnic group or the artistic genius of an ancient, vanished race of Austronesians (see below).
zh: 这些服装进而承载了各种地方意义、价值与用途，它们与国际关系的故事几乎无关，却对原住民社会的社会再生产至关重要。
沿着李仙得红羽纱的流转再往下追踪，可以看到，后来被称为泰雅传统布料的物件，在殖民时期（及之后）又被形形色色的日本人重新挪用于众多目的。作为博物馆藏品、研究对象与纪念品摊上的热门货，泰雅纺织品成了某种象征：要么象征一个特定族群，要么象征一个古老、已消失的南岛人种的艺术天赋（见下文）。

en: Fast-forward to contemporary times: Taiwan Indigenous Peoples have refashioned elements of Japan’s colonial-period repository of material culture. The revival of Atayal weaving practices, partly based on consultation of textiles collected during colonial times and preserved in Japan, now illustrates claims of Atayal distinctiveness and autochthony.
The same can be said for Paiwan, Rukai, and Saisiyat cultural revivals in the post-1980s milieu.
zh: 到了当代，台湾原住民重新改造了日本殖民时期物质文化典藏中的要素。泰雅织布实践的复兴，一部分得益于研究殖民时期收集并保存在日本的纺织品，如今用以支撑泰雅人对自身独特性和本土起源的主张。
1980年代以后，排湾、鲁凯与赛夏文化复兴亦然。

en: As we have seen in the introduction and the first two chapters of this book, indigenes received, in the form of gifts (with strings attached), tons of red cloth—as remnants, garments, bolts, or even flags. We have also seen how the Taiwan Government-General clamped down on gifting by 1900. In the post-Pacification Office dispensation, what LeGendre called “tokens of friendship” were deployed as the candy backed by the whip of trade embargoes and punitive expeditions. During the period of Japan’s “primitive accumulation” of an indigenous storehouse of cultural artifacts, anthropologists entered into these transactions. They wrote about, sketched, photographed, and collected these items, then supplied museums and expositions with evidence of indigenous ethnic integrity, local genius, and archaic vibrancy. Concurrently, trading-post operators accepted Atayal cloth as specie and retailed it to tourists and collectors, diffusing weavings widely to Japanese and international collectors.
zh: 正如我们在本书导论与前两章所见，原住民以礼物（附带条件）的形式收到了成吨的红布，包括布头、成衣、整匹布，甚至旗帜。我们也看到台湾总督府到1900年如何钳制赠礼。在抚垦署撤销以后，李仙得所谓“友谊的表示”成了用来笼络人的甜头，背后有贸易禁运和讨伐作为威胁。在日本对原住民文化文物宝库进行“原始积累”的时期，人类学家介入了这些交易。他们撰文介绍、绘图、拍摄并收集这些物品，然后向博物馆与博览会提供原住民族群完整性、地方创造力与古老活力的证据。与此同时，贸易站经营者把泰雅布当作货币接受，再零售给游客与收藏家，把织物广泛扩散到日本与国际收藏家手中。

en: Much of the indigenous cultural material that was photographed or preserved for posterity was collected during the “lost decade” of Japanese rule (1895–1905), which is usually considered a period of passivity, at worst, or simplistically as one dominated by a policy of “nurture.” However, during this decade, the peoples beyond the savage border who had kept the Qing state at arm’s length dazzled Japanese officials in search of allies and informants with their song, dance, festivals, folktales, and handicrafts. Indigenous emissaries to feasts and parleys posed for photographs and paintings; indigenous artifacts were collected by rural officials in exchange for tobacco and red thread that was subsequently distributed to shore up headmen’s claims to authority; and indigenous textiles purchased in cross-border trade were boxed up and shipped to Japanese museums and industrial expositions to line the pockets and enhance the profiles of Japanese anthropologists (see
). These myriad transactions had the cumulative effect of institutionalizing a view of indigenes as racially and culturally distinct from each other and from Han Taiwanese.
zh: 被拍摄或为后世保存下来的原住民文化材料，大部分是在日本统治的“失落十年”（1895—1905）收集的；这十年通常被视为一段消极时期，更简单的说法则把它概括为以“抚育”政策为主的时期。然而在这十年里，那些把清朝国家拒于门外的“生番界”之外的族群，用他们的歌、舞、节庆、民间故事与手工艺，令寻找盟友与消息提供者的日本官员眼花缭乱。赴宴与谈判的原住民使者摆姿势供拍照与画像；乡村官员用烟草与红线换取原住民文物，这些红线随后被分发出去，帮助头目巩固权威；跨境贸易中购得的原住民纺织品被装箱运往日本的博物馆与工业博览会，以充实日本人类学家的腰包、提升他们的声望（见
）。这无数交易的累积效果，是把一种看法制度化：原住民在种族与文化上彼此不同，也不同于台湾汉人。

en: The contemporary world is politically and economically dominated by settler states and their majority populations.

Therefore, indigenous peoples, for both commercial and political reasons, often find themselves forced to perform identities that meet the expectations of outsiders, whether in court or in the marketplace. Cultural reification was certainly a prominent legacy of Japanese colonial rule in Taiwan. The objects discussed in this chapter, then, remain in play as articles of ethnic pride and as exhibits in the high-stakes game of indigenous renaissance and recovery.
zh: 当代世界在政治与经济上由定居殖民者建立的国家及其多数人口主导。
因此，原住民出于商业与政治双重原因，常常发现自己被迫表演符合外来者期待的身份，无论是在法庭还是在市场。文化的实体化无疑是日本殖民统治在台湾的一项突出遗产。于是，本章讨论的物件仍在发挥作用：既是族群自豪的载体，也是原住民文化复兴和权利恢复这场高风险博弈中的展品。

en: TOKENS OF FRIENDSHIP AND THE INNOCENT ABORIGINE
zh: 友谊的表示与天真无邪的原住民

en: The themes of victimization, trade dependence, and exploitation punctuate descriptions of indigenous-outsider relations from the very first written records about Taiwan. Chen Di’s 1603

) explains that Fujianese traders brought “agates, porcelain, cloth, salt, and brass” to Taiwan to trade for deer horns, hides, and meat. Chen laments that indigenes had “developed some desires” leading “rascals [to] cheat them with junk.”

Two decades later, Commander Cornelis Reyersen observed indigenes exporting diverse animal products for “coarse porcelain and some unbleached linen.” These exports were brokered by the “Chinese living there, who... married local women.”

A February 1624 Dutch East India Company record suggests that trade dependency gave Chinese immigrants near the future Taiwan-fu leverage disproportionate to their numbers: “In almost every house... one, two, three, nay sometimes even five or six Chinese are lodged, whom [indigenes] keep very much under control.... Likewise they themselves are bullied by the Chinese for not giving them food or not working hard enough.

children: The Chinese immediately threaten to deprive them of salt, which means they are dependent on them

zh: 受害、贸易依赖与剥削这些主题，从关于台湾最早的书面记录起，便反复出现在对原住民与外来者关系的描述。陈第1603年的《东番记》（Dongfan Ji）记载，福建商人带“玛瑙、瓷器、布、盐与黄铜”到台湾，换取鹿角、鹿皮与鹿肉。陈第叹惜原住民“滋生了某些欲望”，致使“无赖用劣质货欺骗他们”。
二十年后，指挥官科内利斯·雷耶松观察到原住民出口各种动物产品，换取“粗瓷与一些本色亚麻布”。这些出口由“住在那里的中国人……他们娶了当地女子”居间促成。
1624年2月一份荷兰东印度公司记录表明，贸易依赖使未来台湾府附近的华人移民拥有了与其人数不相称的筹码：“几乎每户人家……都寄宿着一、二、三个，不，有时甚至五六个中国人，〔原住民〕把他们管得很严……同样，他们自己也会因不给中国人食物或干活不够卖力而受中国人欺负。中国人立刻威胁要断他们的盐，这意味着他们依赖中国人。”

en: As we saw in chapter 2, the history of interpreters throughout the Qing period reveals a long record of economic ties that exceeded the boundaries of imperial administration. Jumping ahead to the treaty-port period, we return to the disappearance of fifty-four shipwrecked Ryūkyūans on Taiwan’s southern peninsula in 1871. The calamity brought Meiji Japan’s first official visitors to Taiwan. In particular, the observations of Mizuno Jun merit scrutiny. Mizuno would return to Taiwan as the top civilian official in the Taiwan Government-General at its inception in 1895.
zh: 正如我们在第2章所见，清代通事的历史表明，跨越帝国行政边界的经济联系由来已久。跳到通商口岸时期，我们回到1871年五十四名船难琉球人在台湾南部半岛失踪之事。这场灾难把明治日本首批官方访客带到了台湾。其中，水野遵的观察尤其值得审视。水野后来于1895年台湾总督府创立时，作为最高级文官重返台湾。

en: In 1873, Ambassador Soejima Taneomi dispatched a twenty-two-year-old Mizuno, who was studying Chinese on the continent, from Hong Kong to Danshui to investigate conditions surrounding the deaths of the Ryūkyūans.

Upon arriving at Dakekan, Mizuno’s party trekked eastward on a steep woodcutter’s path toward the so-called savage border. Mizuno was told that areas of Chinese habitation were marked by the russet color of denuded forests, while the indigenous areas were lushly green. Mizuno’s informants told him that this divide ran the length of Taiwan. It was patrolled by armed Han and indigenous guards on either side.
zh: 1873年，副岛种臣大使把正在大陆学汉语、二十二岁的水野，从香港派往淡水，调查琉球人遇害的经过和背景。
抵达大嵙崁后，水野一行沿一条陡峭的樵夫小径东行，朝向所谓的“生番界”。有人告诉水野，汉人居住区以被砍光森林的黄褐色为标记，而原住民区则郁郁葱葱。水野的消息提供者告诉他，这道分界纵贯台湾全岛，两侧由武装的汉人与原住民守卫巡逻。

en: In a clearing used to initiate cross-border parleys, on May 23, 1873, Mizuno hailed a group of passing Atayal people. The men fled to the hills at the sight of Mizuno’s armed Chinese guides. Two Atayal women, however, stayed behind. They explained that their village had been the victim of a ruse. Chinese traders had promised the delivery of Western goods to lure unsuspecting Atayal people into the clearing. The Chinese subsequently kidnapped the Atayal men and ransomed them later in exchange for titles to land. To overcome their reticence, Mizuno offered to distribute large quantities of red cloth, à la LeGendre, if the two women could bring an Atayal headman down from the mountains. Mizuno noted that indigenes coveted red cloth most of all. The next morning, he presented the two women with gifts of red cloth, matches, small daggers, and pearls. That afternoon, the chief sent a different women’s contingent down the mountain. Mizuno supplied each with a “foot or two” of red cloth. Finally, Mizuno presented the chief with a live pig and two large jars of shōchū liquor. With this presentation of “tokens of friendship,” Mizuno had accomplished the “principal goal of his mission, to look into savage strengths and weaknesses, degrees of intelligence and ignorance, and manners and customs.”
zh: 1873年5月23日，在一处用于发起跨境谈判的空地上，水野招呼一群路过的泰雅人。那些男子一见水野的武装汉人向导便逃进山里。然而两名泰雅女子留了下来。她们解释说，自己的村子曾中诡计：汉人商人许诺交付西洋货，把不疑有诈的泰雅人诱入空地，随后绑架泰雅男子，后来索取土地权状才释放他们。为消除对方的戒心，水野提出仿效李仙得，若两名女子能请一位泰雅头目下山，他就赠送大量红布。水野注意到，原住民最想得到红布。次日早晨，他赠给两名女子红布、火柴、小匕首与珍珠。当天下午，头目派了另一批女子下山。水野给每人“一两英尺”红布。最后，水野赠给头目一头活猪与两大罐烧酎。凭借这番“友谊的表示”，水野达成了“此行的主要目标：探察生番的强弱、智愚程度，以及风俗习惯”。

en: Although Mizuno did not record population figures, estimates of military strength, or routes to interior villages (as later travelers would), the intelligence he collected on his mission to Dakekan was put to use a quarter century later. Every transaction in Mizuno’s account was premised on the Dakekan peoples’ desire to obtain imported goods—twenty-two years before the onset of Japanese colonial rule. At the same time, as first governor-general Kabayama Sukenori’s civil administrator, Mizuno issued proclamations and oversaw policies based on his estimation that the
(raw savages, i.e., unassimilated) were generally victims of the cunning and duplicitous Han Taiwanese.
zh: 虽然水野没有记录人口数字、军力估计或通往内陆村落的路线（后来的旅行者会记录），他在大嵙崁之行收集的情报，却在四分之一世纪后派上了用场。水野记述中的每一笔交易，都以大嵙崁人渴望获得进口货为前提——这比日本殖民统治开始早了二十二年。与此同时，作为首任总督桦山资纪的文官行政主管，水野发布公告、监督政策，其依据是他的判断：生番（seiban，即未同化者）一般是狡猾、不守信用的台湾汉人的受害者。

en: George Taylor, an imperial maritime customs agent for the British crown, attested to the popularity of red woolens in southern Taiwan during the same era. Taylor observed that the red color alone made the cloth desirable, since the brightness achieved by Western dyeing techniques could not be achieved by local methods. These “serges,” as they were called, were quickly pulled apart and combined with sturdier local ramie, hemp, and china-grass fiber to make durable clothing. Taylor complained that for everyday use, Taiwanese weaves were still dominating the market, much to the embarrassment of the British official, who had hoped that his machine-made cloth would flood the market.
zh: 乔治·泰勒——为英国王室效力的海关人员——证实了同一时期红色毛料在南台湾的流行。泰勒观察到，单是红色就使布料令人向往，因为西方染色技术达到的鲜艳度，是当地方法无法企及的。这些被称为“哔叽”（serges）的布料很快被拆开，与当地较结实的苎麻、大麻及中国草（china grass，苎麻的一种）的纤维混织，做成耐穿的服装。泰勒抱怨说，就日常使用而言，台湾织物仍主导市场，令这位英国官员大为尴尬——他本指望自己的机织布充斥市场。

en: Ueno Sen’ichi’s 1891 report (see chapter 1) stated that purchasing presents for the indigenes was most necessary for entering the savage territory. Accordingly, Ueno brought along “liquor, tobacco, glass beads, Western red-dyed thread, brass buttons, white ceramic buttons, and so on.” Like so many Japanese officials who followed him, Ueno insisted that presents to indigenes be distributed equally, from the youngest child to the paramount chief. If one indigene were treated too kindly and another too carelessly, hard feelings would result, wrote Ueno. In return for these “tokens of friendship,” chief Watan Yūra produced sweet potatoes and a bundle of rice stalks from a “head-carrying bag” and presented them to Ueno. After this exchange of gifts, Ueno’s mission ended. He concluded that Atayal people were simple and trusting, but they were also quick to anger and never forgot a slight.
zh: 上野专一1891年的报告（见第1章）说，为原住民购买礼物是进入蕃地最必要之事。因此，上野随身带了“酒、烟草、玻璃珠、西洋染红线、黄铜纽扣、白瓷纽扣等等”。像后来众多日本官员一样，上野坚持给原住民的礼物要平均分配，从最幼的孩子到最高头目。上野写道，若一个原住民受优待、另一个受怠慢，就会生出嫌隙。作为对这些“友谊的表示”的回报，头目瓦丹有洛从一个“头驮袋”里掏出甘薯与一捆稻秆，赠给上野。这次赠礼之后，上野的访问结束。他总结说，泰雅人淳朴而信任他人，但也易怒，且从不忘记所受轻慢。

en: Like Ueno, Captain Watanabe, during the previously discussed August 29, 1895, mission to Dakekan, distributed gifts equally among Atayal emissaries to a diplomatic meeting. According to Watanabe’s report, Atayal valued manufactured goods highly, as they swaddled the empty liquor vessels, great and small, into bundles to carry back to their villages (see
). Yet the chief showed no interest in the silver coins he was given.
Hashiguchi Bunzō’s follow-up mission also commenced with the distribution of red cloth, tinned meat, handkerchiefs, ornamental hairpins, short daggers, tobacco, and alcohol.

Hashiguchi wrote that the Jiaobanshan embassy men were adorned with trademark Atayal red-striped capes. Hashiguchi emphasized the importance of red serge (a rough woolen), which he distributed in equal shares. To produce the distinctive red garments, Hashiguchi reported, the women took the serge apart and wove the dyed thread together with locally produced ramie fiber.
zh: 与上野一样，渡边上尉在前述1895年8月29日的大嵙崁之行中，把礼物平均分配给赴会商谈的泰雅使者。据渡边的报告，泰雅人高度重视制成品，因为他们把大小空酒器都裹成捆，背回村里（见
）。然而头目对给他的银币却毫无兴趣。
桥口文藏的随后的出访也以分发红布、罐头肉、手帕、装饰发簪、短匕首、烟草与酒开场。
桥口写道，角板山使团人员披着标志性的泰雅红条纹披风。桥口强调红哔叽（一种粗毛料）的重要性，他按等份分发。桥口报告说，为做出那些独特的红衣，女子们把哔叽拆开，把拆下的染色毛线与当地出产的苎麻纤维混织。

en: Based on his experience with the Jiaobanshan emissaries, Hashiguchi, as director of the Office of Industrial Promotion (

), proposed that each Japanese garrison near the savage border stock gifts for distribution to neighboring tribes. The Civil Affairs Bureau accordingly sent memoranda to the subprefects of Tainan, Miaoli, Yunlin, Yilan, Hengchun, and Puli explaining their importance. It specified that scarlet cotton fabric, red beads, flower hairpins, cigars, daggers, red blankets, red serge, and hand towels were all to be stocked. Every item on the proposed inventory matched one that was distributed by Hashiguchi to the Dakekan emissaries three days earlier, on September 8, 1895.
zh: 基于与角板山使者打交道的经验，桥口作为殖产部（Shokusan-bu）部长，提议“生番界”附近每处日军驻地都储备礼物，分发给邻近部落。民政局因此向台南、苗栗、云林、宜兰、恒春、埔里的支厅长发出备忘录，说明储备这些礼物的重要性。备忘录规定，猩红棉布、红珠、花簪、雪茄、匕首、红毯、红哔叽与手巾都要备办。拟议清单上的每一件物品，都与三天前——1895年9月8日——桥口分发给大嵙崁使者的物品相符。

en: As recounted in chapter 1, after the Pacification Office was opened in mid-1896, station chiefs were ordered to meet with headmen on appointed days and distribute presents. The belief that indigenes treasured their gifts and would do just about anything to receive them informed the office’s optimistic charge. With bolts of red cloth, bags of salt, and bottles of sake as inducements, these hundred men would survey the political, demographic, mineral, vegetative, and military strength of some seven-hundred-odd settlements in uncharted territory.
zh: 如第1章所述，1896年年中抚垦署设立后，各署长奉命在指定日子与头目会面、分发礼物。相信原住民珍视礼物、会为得到它们几乎做任何事，这种信念使当局对抚垦署的任务抱有乐观预期。凭借整匹红布、袋装盐与瓶装清酒作诱因，这一百人将调查地图尚未标明的地区上七百余处聚落的政治、人口、矿产、植被状况和军事实力。

en: In addition to having power as political and diplomatic implements, red-dyed textiles were also known as inducements to commence trade relationships. On September 30, 1895, an anonymous Civil Affairs Bureau translator (tsūyakukan) told a Japanese metropolitan readership that adroit gifting could open Taiwan’s interior to Japanese camphor merchants. The cost of gifts to chiefs was about one yen per camphor tree in Miaoli, he reported. These gifts included red, black, brown, or purple cloth scraps for women and guns, swords, sake, and tobacco for men. To obtain the camphor trees, he wrote, local Chinese also traded Nanjing coins or rings and bracelets made of pearl and lead. The selling price of a camphor tree was sixty or seventy yen—a more than sixtyfold return on investment. This particular correspondent surmised that indigenes did not understand the value of currency or the difference between silver and gold. He wrote that they accepted one or the other based on color preferences for yellow or white and that one could even use shards of glass or chunks of metal for currency in some areas.
zh: 染红的织品能用于政治和外交，也常用来促成贸易往来。1895年9月30日，一位民政局匿名通译官（tsūyakukan）告诉日本本土的读者，巧妙赠礼能为日本樟脑商人打开台湾内陆。他报告说，在苗栗，给头目的礼物成本约为每棵樟脑树一日元。这些礼物包括给女子的红、黑、棕、紫布头，以及给男子的枪、刀、清酒与烟草。他写道，为得到樟脑树，当地中国人还用南京钱，或珍珠与铅制的戒指手镯交易。一棵樟脑树的售价是六七十日元——约为所送礼物价值的六七十倍。这位通讯员推测，原住民不懂货币的价值，也不懂银与金的区别。他写道，他们依对白色或黄色的偏好，选择收银或收金，在某些地区甚至可以用玻璃碎片或金属块当货币。

en: In October 1895 Ueno Sen’ichi’s 1891 report resurfaced in a commercial guide published by the Japanese Ministry of Agriculture and Commerce in Tokyo. The guide reiterated Ueno’s advocacy of red cloth as a rain-making gift and as the price of entry to the “savage territory.” Moreover, it duly reproduced Ueno’s capsule history of Han aggression, which partly attributed land dispossession to the supposed indigenous character traits of simplicity, illiteracy, and lack of foresight. The Chinese, according to this iteration of Ueno’s now recycled report (itself a distillation of translated, paraphrased, and plagiarized passages from Western travelers), were greedy, cunning, and unscrupulous.
zh: 1895年10月，上野专一1891年的报告在东京日本农商务省出版的一本商业指南中重新浮现。指南重申上野对红布的倡导：既是能打开交易局面的礼物，也是进入“蕃地”的入场代价。此外，它还照录上野对汉人侵占原住民土地的简短叙述，把土地剥夺部分归因于据称原住民的性格特征：淳朴、不识字、缺乏远见。按上野这份如今被回收的报告（它本身由若干译自、转述自乃至抄自西方旅行者记述的段落汇编而成）的这一版本，中国人贪婪、狡猾、肆无忌惮。

en: A November 1896 report issued by the Industrial Promotion Section began its discussion of camphor with a predictable admonition that travelers stock “liquor-meat-cloth,” especially Western imported red-dyed cloth. It then excoriated the residents of Beipu as dishonest indigenes to justify stationing armed guards in the area to protect camphor workers. In addition, countering the economic innocence argument, the report announced that indigenous headmen in Qing times required frequent cash payments, in addition to feasts and gifts, to keep the peace.
zh: 殖产部1896年11月发布的一份报告，以一句可预见的告诫开始讨论樟脑：旅行者要备办“酒—肉—布”，尤其是西洋进口染红布。接着它痛斥北埔居民为不诚实的原住民，以便为在当地派驻武装守卫保护樟脑工人辩护。此外，为反驳原住民不谙交易的说法，报告宣布，清代原住民头目除宴请与礼物外，还会要求对方经常支付现金，以此作为维持和平的条件。

en: A series of internal memoranda from the Luodong (Yilan) section chief for aborigine affairs also engaged in the rhetoric of indigenous victimization in commerce. He urged honest, fair-dealing Japanese immigrants to insert themselves into the “aborigine trade.” If they didn’t, he warned, the profits would remain in the hands of unscrupulous Chinese who set off violent cycles of revenge feuds by cheating Xitou and Nan’ao peoples.
The Luodong office claimed to have brokered marriages between the commercially minded

(acculturated savages) of Alishi village and daughters of the Atayal Nan’ao villages to strengthen government ties with the mountain peoples. The district office held a large wedding banquet at which over a hundred Nan’ao Atayal guests were feted in May 1899. The Japanese official also encouraged the adoption of indigenous males into

households in order to recruit these bicultural couples to act as interpreters. Qualifying the stereotype of Atayal disinterest in material gain, this scheme was premised on the lure of trade goods and wealth to inspire the Nan’ao villagers to place their daughters and sons among the trading villages at the foot of the mountains.
zh: 罗东（宜兰）蕃务课长的一系列内部备忘录，也运用了原住民在商业中受害的辞令。他敦促诚实、公平交易的日本移民介入“蕃人贸易”。他警告说，若不如此，利润就会留在肆无忌惮的中国人手中，他们欺骗溪头和南澳人，引发一轮又一轮的暴力报复。

罗东厅署声称曾居间促成有商业头脑的阿里史村熟蕃（jukuban，已接受外来文化的蕃人）与泰雅南澳各村女儿的婚姻，以加强政府与山地民族的联系。1899年5月，厅署举办了一场大型婚宴，款待一百多名南澳泰雅宾客。这位日本官员还鼓励把原住民男子收养进熟蕃家庭，以招募这些熟悉两种文化的夫妇充当通事。这一方案也给泰雅人不求物质利益的刻板印象打了折扣。它指望用货品和财富吸引南澳村民，使他们愿意让子女在山脚经营贸易的村落安家。

en: As we have seen, Japanese accounts of diplomatic gifting repeatedly insisted that indigenes were acutely sensitive to “equal distribution,” whether it was equal measures of cloth or portions of boiled meat. It is hard to discount such reports as projections or stereotypes, since they exist in so many forms. But did such behavior mean that indigenes were egalitarian, unselfish, and innocent of the profit motive?
zh: 如我们所见，日本关于外交赠礼的记述反复坚持，原住民对“平均分配”高度敏感，无论是等量的布还是等份的煮肉。很难把这类报告当作投射或刻板印象而不予理会，因为多种形式的记录都有这种描述。但这种行为是否意味着原住民主张平等、无私，且不追求获利？

en: At distribution events, a Japanese official could proclaim that his emperor would not play favorites. In kind, indigenous emissaries equally distributed goods among their own followers, at least in the presence of Japanese officials. But these happy structural isomorphisms had their limits. According to infantryman Irie Takeshi, Puli prefect Hiyama Tetsusaburō doled out the expected blankets and jars of liquor at his wedding to the daughter of the Paalan chief near Wushe. Complications arose, however, when Hiyama, unable to distinguish Toda and Truku men from the Paalan men, distributed gifts to everyone. Angered by the fact that their rivals from Toda and Truku received gifts, the Wushe men ambushed them after the banquet and took their gifts at gunpoint. Irie reported that the Wushe men asserted their right to receive the gifts first and then to redistribute them to other locals as they saw fit. After all, their chief had conducted a marriage alliance with Hiyama.

Hiyama’s successor in Puli, Nagano Yoshitora, triggered the same response by distributing presents to Toda emissaries after a feast in 1898. On their way back home, the Toda men were ambushed by Wushe men. In the ensuing battle, Toda and Wushe suffered fifteen and two casualties, respectively.
zh: 在分配场合，日本官员可以宣称他的天皇不偏袒。同样，原住民使者也在自己的追随者中平均分配货物，至少在日本官员在场时如此。但这些看似相契合的分配方式有其限度。据步兵入江武说，埔里厅长桧山铁三郎在娶雾社附近芭兰头目之女的婚礼上，按惯例分送了毯子和坛装酒。然而复杂情况出现了：桧山分不清都达、德路固男子与芭兰男子，便给所有人都分了礼物。雾社人因对手都达、德路固人也收到礼物而愤怒，宴后伏击他们，持枪夺走了礼物。入江报告说，雾社人主张自己有权先接受礼物，再随己意把它们重新分配给其他当地人。毕竟，他们的头目与桧山缔结了婚姻联盟。
桧山在埔里的继任者长野义虎，1898年一次宴后给都达使者分发礼物，引发了同样的反应。都达人回家途中被雾社人伏击。在随后的战斗中，都达与雾社分别伤亡十五人与两人。

en: Moreover, detailed lists of gift items in the manuscript records of traveling district officials reveal that more expensive gifts were earmarked for headmen. These unequal distributions were, in fact, routine.

In summary, some individuals and groups of indigenes did not view material goods as fungible commodities that could be reduced to a value expressed in monetary terms. Nonetheless, these goods were still highly valued, were sites of contestation and competition, and were deployed by indigenes as either commodities or political currency.
zh: 此外，地方官巡视时所作的手写记录中详细的礼物清单揭示，更贵重的礼物是指定给头目的。这种不平等分配实际上是常规。
总之，有些原住民个体与群体并不把物质货物视为可相互替代、可以货币衡量其价值的商品。尽管如此，这些货物仍被高度重视，成为争夺和竞争的对象，并被原住民用作商品或政治通货。

en: TRADING POSTS, BEHAVIOR MODIFICATION, AND PUNITIVE EMBARGOES
zh: 贸易站、行为规训与惩罚性禁运

en: Saitō Otosaku, Pacification Office chief in Linyipu, articulated the growing chorus of criticisms directed at Hashiguchi’s gifting policy in an 1898 white paper. In his preface, Saitō wrote: “One must take care in distributing gifts to the indigenes; if it is done carelessly, it can lead to feelings of injustice and foment anger, or it can cause lethargy and shiftlessness... We must not distribute gifts without a reason; we must certainly not distribute luxury goods; we must not give in to demands for goods; when gifts are requested, we should give no more than is absolutely necessary.”
zh: 林圮埔抚垦署署长齐藤音作，在1898年一份白皮书中表达了针对桥口赠礼政策日益高涨的批评声浪。他在序言中写道：“给原住民分发礼物必须谨慎；若草率从事，可能让人觉得受到不公对待、激起愤怒，或导致懈怠与游手好闲……我们不可无缘无故分发礼物；绝不可分发奢侈品；不可屈从于对货物的索求；当有人索要礼物时，我们给的绝不应超过必要的数量。”

en: In language that reflects a newfound confidence in the Japanese government’s ability to command rather than placate, Saitō composed a well-calibrated scale of gift categories. He reserved the Hashiguchi-style “tokens of friendship” for first-time visitors to government offices. Return “guests” would have to earn their gifts. For example, to receive goods classified in Saitō’s top-shelf categories, indigenes would have to perform “labor on roadwork, afforestation projects, or stock-raising/farming enterprises... or service as savage auxiliaries (

).” Such efforts would be rewarded with “thick cotton shirts; black cloth, light cloth, table salt, matches, and so on”; “buttons, all colors of wool thread, combs, tobacco, Nanjing pearls, and so on”; and, for especially meritorious service, guns and ammunition.
zh: 齐藤用的语言，反映出日本政府有了直接发号施令的底气，无须再一味安抚；他仔细划分了礼物的等级。他把桥口式“友谊的表示”保留给首次来访政府机关的人。回头“客”则必须自己挣得礼物。例如，要领取齐藤最高档类别的货物，原住民就得从事“道路工程、造林工程，或畜牧或农业事业中的劳作……或充当蕃兵（banhei）”。这类出力将获赏“厚棉衫；黑布、浅色布、食盐、火柴等等”；“纽扣、各色毛线、梳子、烟草、南京珠等等”；以及，特别有功者可获赏枪械和弹药。

en: Saitō recommended that farm tools, seeds, and stock be freely given because they would wean the indigenes from their hunting economy. He argued that firearms and ammunition, though necessary for the time being, should be phased out, because hunting in and of itself was a vestige of savagery. Saitō also envisioned the government-managed trade as a source of profit. Lesser categories in Saitō’s typology, which ranged from hoes and hatchets to hairpins and fans painted with
scenes, were to be stocked as trade items.
zh: 齐藤建议免费给予农具、种子与牲畜，因为它们能使原住民脱离狩猎经济。他论证说，火器弹药虽暂时还要供应，却应逐步停止供应，因为狩猎本身是野蛮的残余。齐藤还把政府管理的贸易设想为利润来源。他所列的其余较低等级物品——从锄头、短柄斧到发簪、绘有锦绘（nishiki-e）图案的扇子——则应备作交易货品。

en: A plan that may have been influenced by Saitō’s report was implemented in Yilan in mid-1901. It restricted trade to government-licensed agents who would operate with set exchange rates. For example, one deer pelt was listed as equivalent to two feet of red woolen cloth or nine catties of table salt; one bear bladder equaled two iron pots or one suckling pig; three catties of wood ears equaled five catties of salt or a skein of thread; and so on. The government would profit from this trade and use the proceeds for “indigenous betterment,” which meant building schools and transporting and lodging chiefs’ families who came down the mountain to enroll in the pilot education programs.
The conversion of gift-distribution centers into trading posts was central to the trade-for-education program attempted in Yilan in 1901 (see

). While these projects can be understood as attempts to give indigenes a “fair shake” vis-à-vis their wealthier Han neighbors, these trading posts quickly turned into instruments of punishment, conquest, and income generation for the Japanese state.
zh: 一项可能受齐藤报告影响的计划，于1901年年中在宜兰实施。它把贸易限于政府许可的代理人，按固定兑换率经营。例如，一张鹿皮列为相当于两英尺红色毛料或九斤食盐；一个熊膀胱等于两口铁锅或一头乳猪；三斤木耳等于五斤盐或一绞线，诸如此类。政府将从这项贸易获利，并把收益用于“改善原住民处境”，即建学校，以及接送下山参加试办教育项目的头目家属并安排住宿。
把礼物分配中心转化为贸易站，是1901年宜兰试行的以贸易换教育计划的核心（见
）。这些举措可视为尝试让原住民在和较富裕的汉人邻居打交道时得到“公平待遇”。这些贸易站却很快变成了日本国家惩罚、征服与创收的工具。
