en: In 1899 Gotō Shinpei launched the Taiwan Government-General’s camphor monopoly, along with other measures, to increase revenue to support his vision of an efficiently run surplus-extracting colony. As Antonio Tavares has shown, the official Japanese plan for camphor—to export large quantities of uniform quality with profits accruing to Japanese capitalists—posed a direct threat to the Atayal, Saisiyat, and other northern indigenes, whose leaders were accustomed to leasing forest land, collecting tolls, or organizing production themselves. Accordingly, cases of Atayal and Saisiyat violence against Japanese officials accelerated.

In response, the Pacification Offices were abolished in June 1898, and rural installations for aborigine management began to emphasize the importance of embargoes, smuggling, illicit trade, and contraband. As northern tribes put up stout armed resistance to logging-company encroachments, government officials began to worry less about the injury done to indigenes by crafty Chinese and to express outrage that Han traders would subvert Japanese bans on weapons, ammunition, or even salt to blacklisted tribes.
zh: 1899年，后藤新平启动台湾总督府的樟脑专卖，连同其他措施，以增加收入，实现高效经营殖民地、从中汲取财政盈余的构想。正如安东尼奥·塔瓦雷斯所示，日本官方的樟脑计划——出口大量品质统一的樟脑、利润归日本资本家——对泰雅、赛夏及其他北部原住民构成直接威胁，他们的首领习惯于出租林地、征收通行税或自行组织生产。因此，泰雅与赛夏针对日本官员的武力行动越发频繁。
作为回应，抚垦署于1898年6月被废除，乡村负责理蕃的机构开始着重执行禁运并查缉走私、非法交易及违禁品。随着北部部落顽强地以武力抵抗伐木公司侵入，政府官员开始较少担心狡猾中国人对原住民的伤害，转而表达愤怒：汉人商人竟破坏日本对列入黑名单部落的武器、弹药乃至盐的禁令。

en: Taipei prefectural governor Murakami Yoshio urged that the tribes responsible for a June 1900 armed uprising near Dakekan, which cost over a thousand Chinese and Japanese lives and destroyed much property, be completely cut off from trade and from receiving gifts. Friendly villages would have only a partial ban on trade, in Murakami’s plan. Murakami sent out strict regulations requiring merchants to be registered and calling for a complete ban on commerce in guns and salt to troubled areas. Murakami believed that villages could be crushed and brought to heel after a few months of deprivation of life’s necessities.

In September of the same year, the Balisha district chief in Yilan sent out a similar memorandum, calling for selective trade embargoes against villages who defied the government’s authority. He stipulated that feasting and trade would be permitted for tribes who had made amends for their crimes or who were above suspicion.
zh: 台北知事村上义雄敦促，对1900年6月大嵙崁附近武装起义负责的部落——该起义造成一千多名中国人和日本人死亡、毁坏大量财产——应完全切断贸易与接受礼物。按村上的计划，友好村落只受部分贸易禁令。村上发出严格规章，要求商人登记，并呼吁完全禁止向动乱地区出售枪械和盐。村上相信，剥夺生活必需品几个月后，村落就会被压垮、制服。
同年9月，宜兰巴里沙课长发出类似备忘录，呼吁对反抗政府权威的村落实施选择性贸易禁运。他规定，已经为过错作出补偿或未受怀疑的部落，仍可参加宴会和贸易。

en: Such a policy might have seemed wildly optimistic in the era when Ueno and Hashiguchi were being led by their guides into terra incognita to purchase interviews with “demanding” headmen and chiefs. Yet, by 1900, by following the Pacification Office’s directive to regularly supply gifts to headmen as an incentive to “heed invitations to arrive and be transformed,” the Yilan district offices rerouted enough traffic or created enough new demand to be in a position to open and close the spigot.
zh: 在上野与桥口被向导带入未知之地、花费礼物才得以会见“索求甚多”的大小头目的时代，这样的政策或许显得盲目乐观。然而到1900年，通过遵循抚垦署定期向头目供给礼物、以激励其“听从召唤前来归化”的指令，宜兰厅署已经改变了相当多贸易的流向，或创造出足够大的新需求，因而掌握了放行或切断交易的权力。

en: In 1902 two major developments conspired to minimize the centrality of the diplomatic and pedagogical functions of “entangled objects” and accentuate the punitive power of their regulation. First, the Ri Aguai Rebellion, which pitted an indigenous–Hakka–Han coalition of camphor producers against the government-general, taught the Japanese that force would be required to make northern Taiwan’s interior safe for capitalism. Under Ri Aguai’s domination, camphor production was too decentralized, too beholden to toll-state politics that ran on bribes, and too unproductive to meet the camphor monopoly’s requirements for black ink on the annual balance sheet of colonial management.

Second, Gotō Shinpei, through a combination of adroit manipulation and cold-blooded assassination, brought the Japanese campaign against armed Han resistance to completion that same year. In late 1902 an Indigenous Affairs Section was placed under the Police Bureau.
zh: 1902年，两项重大发展共同作用，使“纠缠之物”的外交和教化作用退居其次，凸显了管制这些物品的惩罚作用。第一，李阿乖起义使一个原住民—客家—汉人樟脑生产者联盟对抗总督府，这让日本人认定，要在北台湾内陆保障资本主义经营，必须动用武力。在李阿乖支配下，樟脑生产太分散、太受制于仰赖贿赂运作的关卡型政体、太低产，难以通过樟脑专卖使殖民地的年度账面有盈余。
第二，后藤新平通过巧妙操纵与冷血暗杀相结合，同年完成了日本对汉人武装抵抗的征伐。1902年末，一个蕃务课被置于警务局之下。

en: In July 1905 Government Order 56 strictly regulated all “aborigine trade” merchants. Although private traders were still allowed to operate, they required government permits. All trade items were to be registered and declared, along with the names of all employees and coworkers.

The long list of surrender ceremonies that punctuate the annals of aborigine administration after 1906 shows that resumption of borderland trade was important to indigenous leaders. In January 1906 the four villages of Fanshuliao (Ahou Prefecture) promised not to seek contraband trade goods from camphor workers on the savage border as a condition of resuming trade. In May 1906 the Wushe (Tgdaya) tribes agreed to leave their weapons at home to conduct business at trading posts and to stay at specially designated lodgings during sojourns for commerce.
zh: 1905年7月，府令第56号严格规管所有“蕃人贸易”商人。虽然私人商人仍获准经营，却需要政府许可。所有贸易物品都要登记申报，连同所有雇员与合作人员的姓名。
1906年以后，理蕃纪事里屡次记载的归顺仪式表明，恢复边疆贸易对原住民首领很重要。1906年1月，番薯寮（阿猴厅）四村承诺不向“生番界”上的樟脑工人寻求禁售货物，作为恢复贸易的条件。1906年5月，雾社（德固达雅）部落同意把武器留在家中、到贸易站做生意，并在经商逗留期间住在特别指定的宿处。

en: In the summer of 1909, the government-general put strict embargoes and rations at the center of its much publicized “Five-Year Plan to Subdue the Indigenes.” On October 9, 1909, after applying for terms of surrender, certain Dakekan tribes were permitted “one rice-bowl of salt per month per person” as “gifts,” though not as “trade items.” The tribes agreed to cease taking heads, to surrender their guns, and to submit to biannual inspections for weapons. Toda’s terms of surrender on October 17, 1909, also stipulated that indigenes could not negotiate the price of goods at the reopened trading posts. Moreover, matches, salt, and daggers would be excluded from the list of trade items and supplied as gifts to Toda residents in amounts determined by the government-general. The following day, the Malepa tribes submitted to similar terms, accepting a ban on trade in salt, matches, and daggers in exchange for subsistence-level handouts. On November 11, 1909, the Xalut tribes also surrendered, again foreswearing the right to trade in salt, matches, and daggers.
zh: 1909年夏，总督府把严格禁运与配给置于其大肆宣传的“五年理蕃计划”的中心。1909年10月9日，大嵙崁一些部落在请求议定投降条件之后，获准“每人每月一碗盐”作为“礼物”，而非“贸易物品”。这些部落同意停止猎首、交出枪械、接受每年两次的武器检查。都达1909年10月17日的投降条件还规定，原住民不得在重开的贸易站议价。此外，火柴、盐、匕首将被排除在贸易物品清单之外，按总督府决定的数量作为礼物供给都达居民。次日，马赫坡部落归顺于类似条件，接受盐、火柴、匕首的贸易禁令，以换取仅够维持生计的配给。1909年11月11日，白狗部落也投降，再次放弃盐、火柴、匕首的贸易权。

en: On April 1, 1910, the government-general began to operate its own trading posts, instead of merely supervising trade. The management of this trade was entrusted to the Taiwan branch of the Patriotic Women’s League (

while the former system of privately run licensed trading posts remained as a parallel system operated by Han Taiwanese. Echoing Saitō Otosaku’s memorandum of 1897, this system announced its intention to reform indigenous character by suppressing the instinct to hunt.

Special commissioner Marui Keijirō inspected these trading posts in 1913 and urged that the Women’s League be stripped of the contracts (and that private trading posts be abolished, as well). In a painstakingly detailed accounting of exchange rates for adzuki beans and salt rations, among other commodities, Marui pointed out that the Women’s League was fleecing the indigenes. He believed, consistent with earlier reports about Han avarice, that such unfair dealing would provoke anger in the long run. Marui argued against the participation of Chinese merchants on the grounds that their bad moral character was corrupting by its very nature. He even linked the presence of venereal disease among indigenes to Chinese traders. As a substitute, he recommended the Saitō plan as the only way forward: use indigenous consumer appetites and trade dependency as a lever to reform indigenous character through the promotion of weaving, planting, and stock breeding.
zh: 1910年4月1日，总督府开始自营贸易站，而非仅监督贸易。这项贸易的管理被委托给爱国妇人会（Aikoku Fujinkai）台湾支部，
而旧的私营许可贸易站体制则作为由台湾汉人经营的平行体制保留。呼应齐藤音作1897年的备忘录，这套制度宣称要压制原住民的狩猎本能，以改变他们的性格。

特派委员丸井圭治郎1913年视察这些贸易站，敦促撤销妇人会的经营合同，并废除私营贸易站。在对红豆、盐配给及其他商品兑换率极其详细的核算中，丸井指出妇人会的交易条件在盘剥原住民。他与早年那些指责汉人贪婪的报告持相同看法，认为这种不公平交易长远会激起愤怒。丸井反对华人商人参与，理由是其道德败坏就本质而言具有腐蚀性。他甚至把原住民中的性病与华人商人联系起来。作为替代，他推荐齐藤方案为唯一出路：利用原住民的消费欲望与贸易依赖作杠杆，通过促进织布、种植、畜牧来改造原住民性格。

en: A heavy hand was required, Marui argued, because indigenes were still mentally deficient in terms of their capacity to function as economic moderns. For example, Marui suggested that they be paid only in tools or other durable goods instead of cash for labor on roads and other public works. Why? They might foolishly spend their wages. Marui expressed frustration that indigenes hiked kilometers of mountain trails to save six thousandths of a yen on a catty of salt. He attributed this stubbornness to the well-known desire of indigenes to be treated fairly—if salt cost 5 sen per catty in Wushe, he wrote, then Toda men would not pay 5.6 sen for it at the nearest trading post but would instead walk all the way to Wushe to get the “fair price.”
zh: 丸井论证说，必须严格管束原住民，因为他认为，原住民的心智能力仍不足以在现代经济中独立行事。例如，丸井建议，道路及其他公共工程的劳役，只用工具或其他耐用品支付，而非现金。为什么？他们会把工资胡乱花掉。让丸井感到无奈的是，有些原住民会为了买一斤盐省下千分之六日元，走上几公里山路。他把这种固执归因于原住民众所周知的、要求公平对待的渴望——他写道，若雾社盐每斤5钱，都达人就不会在最近贸易站付5.6钱，而会一路走到雾社去拿“公平价格”。

en: Soon after Marui’s report was released in October 1914, Government Order 85 called for the establishment of official trading posts to replace the Women’s League institutions. These posts would be operated by police captains (
) and assistant captains (

), who would report to district heads. All posts would work with fixed barter schedules, to be set at the prefectural level. Following Marui’s plan nearly to the letter, the circular that accompanied the new trading-post regulations stated:
zh: 丸井报告1914年10月发布后不久，府令第85号要求设立官营贸易站，取代妇人会机构。这些站点将由警部（keibu）与警部补（keibu-ho）经营，向地方行政长官报告。所有站点都按固定的易货比价表交易，具体比价由各厅制定。几乎逐字遵循丸井方案，伴随新贸易站规章的通令写道：

en: The goal of trade in the indigenous territory is completely for education. To have success, we will pay high prices for cereals, legumes, ramie, rattan, and wicker goods; we will sell farming implements and pig and cattle stock at low prices. We want to instill an agricultural ethos among them. We will pay low prices for deer antlers, deer penis, animal pelts, and bones, to discourage hunting.
zh: 蕃地贸易的目标完全在于教育。为求成功，我们将高价收购谷物、豆类、苎麻、藤与藤编器；低价出售农具与供饲养的猪牛。我们要在他们中间灌输一种重农观念。我们将低价收购鹿角、鹿鞭、兽皮与骨头，以抑制狩猎。

en: Moreover, villages that are not submissive will have their rations of salt severely limited. If we interrupt the flow of salt, that will give them some time to reflect upon their situation. This is a way to exercise coercion without resorting to brute force. It is a “soft policy.” We are willing to sacrifice profit for the government to attain our goal of making the indigenes into farmers.
zh: 此外，不顺从的村落，食盐配给将大幅削减。若我们中断盐的流通，那会给他们一些时间反省自身处境。这是一种不动用蛮力而施行强制的办法。这是一项“柔性政策”。我们愿意让政府少赚利润，以达成把原住民变成农夫的目标。

en: In the short term, the new policy failed to deter hunting. In the February 1917 issue of the government organ

, ethnologist Mori Ushinosuke explained that 70 percent of the value of indigenous “exports” exchanged at trading posts consisted of animal products obtained in the hunt. Mori wrote that indigenes could not afford metal pots, salt, or fabrics without hunting. In addition, hunting put meat on the table. Mori highlighted the economic irrationality of indigenous agriculture when prices for crops were so low: at the time of his writing, a deer penis still brought five yen, bear bladders ten yen, and a good set of deer antlers thirty to forty yen in some markets.
In short, a couple of well-aimed shots or smartly set traps was equivalent to months of toil in the fields or on road crews.
zh: 短期内，新政策未能阻止狩猎。在政府机关报《台湾时报》（Taiwan Gazette）1917年2月号上，民族学家森丑之助解释说，原住民在贸易站卖出的货物总值中，70%来自狩猎所得的动物产品。森写道，不狩猎，原住民就买不起金属锅、盐或布料。此外，狩猎也给他们提供肉食。森强调，当作物价格如此低廉时，原住民农业在经济上是非理性的：在他写作时，一条鹿鞭仍能卖五日元，熊膀胱十日元。在某些市场，一副上好的鹿角可卖三四十日元。
简言之，打中几枪，或巧设罗网，所得便抵得上在田里劳作或参加筑路队数月的收入。

en: As we have seen in the foregoing, indigenes were, at least in some contexts, demonstrably motivated by the prospect of cash earnings, material benefit, and personal advantage, according to the records of the Taiwan Government-General itself. But these anecdotal examples, no matter how legion, did little to disrupt the view that indigenes were ipso facto irrational, childlike creatures who lived on the “fruits of the chase” and required tutelage. A 1935 article in a Japanese policemen’s magazine titled “The Economic Sensibilities of Savages and [Savage] Customs” provides but one of many examples of this resilient trope.
zh: 如前所述，据台湾总督府自己的记录，原住民至少在某些情境下，明显受现金收入、物质利益与个人好处的前景驱动。但这些这类个案无论有多少，都几乎未能打破这样一种看法：原住民本质上是靠“猎获物”为生，既不理性，又像孩子一样需要监护。1935年一本日本警察杂志上一篇题为《生番的经济观念与〔生番〕习俗》的文章，不过是这一顽强套话的众多例子之一。

en: It maintained that indigenes did not customarily buy or sell goods based on considerations of market price but instead valued them in accord with traditional value. This estimation was the same one that ruled out the upper Hengchun Paiwanese from being included in the regularly administered territories with the lower Hengchun Paiwanese in 1904 (see chapter 1). With so much home-brewed liquor to be had for free, the article continued, there was little incentive for drink-loving indigenes to worry about having cash on hand. Therefore, they spent their ready cash until they were flat broke. These sweeping generalizations were illustrated with a large photograph of several Tsou men downing bamboo cups of wine with gusto. The author conceded that some indigenes maximized profit and adopted a market mentality, thanks to colonial policies of tutelage. He congratulated the police and hopefully noted that the indigenes were losing their backward habits and becoming more like Japanese.
zh: 它主张，原住民习惯上不是基于市场价格考量买卖货物，而是按传统价值估价。这一判断，与1904年把恒春北部的排湾人排除在普通行政区之外，而将恒春南部的排湾人划入普通行政区的判断如出一辙（见第1章）。文章继续说，既然有这么多自酿酒可免费喝到，好酒的原住民无须为买酒在手头预留现金。因此，他们把现款花到一文不名。这些笼统概括配了一张大照片：几名邹族男子兴致勃勃地用竹杯大口喝酒。作者承认，得益于殖民监护政策，有些原住民已懂得尽可能多地获利，学会按市场规律行事。他祝贺警察，并满怀希望地指出，原住民正在摆脱落后习惯，变得更像日本人。

en: But if indeed some Atayal and Saisiyat farmers were making profits in business, it is hard to see how Japanese policies were to thank for this result. Imposed trade dependency, embargoes on necessities, fixed prices at the trading posts, and an onerous licensing system were not aimed at producing profit-seeking, utility-maximizing individuals but rather hard-working, surplus-producing, and pacified imperial subjects.
zh: 但即便确有一些泰雅与赛夏农夫在生意上获利，也很难看出这结果该归功于日本政策。强加的贸易依赖、必需品禁运、贸易站的固定价格，以及严苛的许可制度，其目标不是造就逐利、效用最大化的个体，而是勤劳、能创造剩余产出、服从当局的帝国臣民。

en: TEXTILES IN EXPOSITIONS, MUSEUMS, AND PHOTOGRAPHS
zh: 博览会、博物馆与照片中的纺织品

en: Colonial-period writers, especially officials, considered the early years of the occupation to have been ones of passivity regarding aborigine policy. Outposts were lightly staffed and underfunded, to be sure. Moreover, most of the government’s resources were poured into the war against the so-called “bandits” (

) from 1896 through 1903—who were mostly nonindigenous, as far as the Japanese could tell. Therefore, there is some truth to the view that the era of “red-cloth diplomacy” was a historical cul-de-sac. But for the ethnologists whose taxonomic work, photography, collecting, and display efforts are still bearing fruit in Atayal ethnic revival movements, the years 1895–1903 were remembered as a golden age.
zh: 殖民时期的作者，尤其是官员，认为占领早年在蕃人政策上是消极的。诚然，前哨人手不足、经费不足。此外，1896年至1903年，政府大部分资源都投入了对所谓“土匪”（dohi）的战争——据日本人所知，这些人大多不是原住民。因此，认为“红布外交”时代是一条历史死胡同，这种看法并非全无依据。但对那些民族学家而言——他们的分类工作、摄影、收藏与筹办展览的工作，时至今日仍为泰雅族群复兴运动所借重——1895年至1903年被铭记为一段黄金时代。

en: To bring our story full circle, then, we return to the National Taiwan Museum, site of the

exhibition. The revered aborigine expert Mori Ushinosuke was the first curator of the indigenous materials at the museum, and he left a long shadow. Mori was an interpreter for Tokyo University anthropologist Torii Ryūzō, who made four anthropological surveys of Taiwan between 1896 and 1900. Mori was also a junior contemporary and sometime rival of the famous historian, folklorist, ethnologist, and taxonomist Inō Kanori (1867–1925), a formidable collector in his own right. To this day, Mori Ushinosuke’s ethnographic photographs are prominently displayed in the National Taiwan Museum’s permanent exhibition and in other Taiwanese museums. Along with Inō’s and Torii’s collected materials, photographs, and biographical information, these collectors and the artifacts that contributed to ethnology are often celebrated and, to the best of my knowledge, the collectors are rarely considered as plunderers or exploiters of indigenous heritage.
zh: 那么，为使我们的故事回到原点，我们回到国立台湾博物馆，《彩虹与蜻蜓》展览的所在地。备受推崇的原住民研究专家森丑之助是该馆首任原住民藏品策展人，他留下了长远影响。森曾担任东京大学人类学家鸟居龙藏的译员，后者在1896年至1900年间对台湾作了四次人类学调查。森也是著名历史学家、民俗学家、民族学家兼分类学家伊能嘉矩（1867—1925）的年纪较轻的同行，有时彼此竞争。伊能本人也是一位颇具实力的收藏家。至今，森丑之助的民族志照片仍醒目地陈列在国立台湾博物馆的常设展及其他台湾博物馆中。连同伊能与鸟居收集的材料、照片与传记信息，这些收藏家及那些为民族学作出贡献的文物常被颂扬，而且据我所知，收藏家很少被视为原住民遗产的掠夺者或剥削者。

en: During the first decade of colonial rule, at the pacification outposts, government halls, and army garrisons, these Meiji-period anthropologists photographed, measured, interviewed, and collected artifacts from the indigenous representatives who showed up to receive gifts or have a social drink. Inō Kanori’s field notes, Torii Ryūzō’s published travelogues, and Mori’s serialized memoirs all describe the period as a time when demobilized Japanese soldiers, Han-indigenous interpreters, ethnologists, government officials, and indigenous headmen assembled to conduct business, exchange information, and size each other up.
zh: 殖民统治头十年，在抚垦署据点、政府厅舍和陆军驻地，这些明治时期人类学家为前来接受礼物或饮酒交际的原住民代表拍照，给他们测量、访谈，并从他们手中收集文物。伊能嘉矩的田野笔记、鸟居龙藏出版的游记、森的连载回忆录，都把这一时期描述为这样一个时代：复员日本士兵、通晓汉语与原住民语言的通事、民族学家、政府官员与原住民头目聚集一堂，办事、交换信息、互相打量。

en: In the era before participant observation, anthropologists like Inō worked quickly and gathered evidence opportunistically. Discussions about gift items, as we saw with Hashiguchi’s confused conversations about the loan/gift of blankets to the Jiaobanshan emissaries, acted as prompts to initiate discussions between parties that had very little to discuss, given the language problems that plagued these encounters. The precious materials also functioned as the currency of access.
zh: 在人类学尚未采用参与观察法的年代，伊能这样的人类学家工作迅速、见机收集证据。关于礼物物品的讨论——正如我们在桥口就毯子借／赠给角板山使者的混乱交谈中所见——给双方开启交谈提供了话题，而他们原本因言语不通而很难交谈。这些贵重物件也是取得接触机会的筹码。

en: Inō wrote that in the “course of distributing various items colored red, which they generally like, such as scraps of red cloth, red yarn, red Japanese flags, and ornate hairpins,” he had divined key aspects of the Atayal guests’ mental life (shisō). There are echoes of Ueno Sen’ichi’s 1891 report in Inō’s 1896 update, but there are important differences. Like Ueno, Inō observed a reverence for the gifts, polite manners in receiving them, and a lack of selfishness among the recipients: they insisted that everyone receive the same gifts.
zh: 伊能写道，在“分发他们普遍喜欢的各种红色物品——如红布头、红线、红色日本旗与华丽发簪——的过程中”，他察知泰雅来客思想（shisō）的若干要点。伊能1896年的报告呼应了上野专一1891年报告，但也有重要差异。与上野一样，伊能观察到对礼物的珍视、接受时的礼貌举止，以及受赠者的无私：他们坚持人人得到相同的礼物。

en: But Inō’s report did not compare the Atayal people (as he would later call them) favorably to the Han Taiwanese, nor did he dwell on their simplicity or innocence.

Instead, Inō learned the local names for the numerous types of clothing and adornment that were fashioned from these gifts and illustrated his account with several carefully labeled sketches. Having established that the female visitors from the Wulai area were similar in appearance to the women brought from Dakekan by Hashiguchi in 1895 (see above), Inō classified them as coethnics. To the question, “By what name do you refer to yourselves?,” Inō heard the reply, “Taiyal,” from members of each contingent. Inō recorded this term in Roman script, announcing a new scientific outsider’s perspective on non-Han peoples in Taiwan. As he noted, the Qing terms
and
(literally “raw savages” and “cooked savages”) were externally imposed political categories.
, in contrast, was a self-designated ethnonym, according to Inō.
zh: 但伊能的报告并没有把泰雅人（他后来如此称呼）与台湾汉人作有利比较，也没有着重说他们淳朴或天真。

相反，伊能弄清了用这些礼物制成的各类衣饰在当地的名称，并用几幅仔细标注的素描为他的记述配图。在确定乌来地区的女性访客与1895年桥口从大嵙崁带来的女子外貌相似（见上文）后，伊能把她们归为同族。对“你们用什么名字称呼自己？”这个问题，伊能从每批成员那里听到的回答都是“泰雅”（Taiyal）。伊能用罗马字记录了这个词，标志着来自外部的一种新兴科学视角开始用于研究台湾非汉人群。正如他指出，清代的“生番”和“熟番”（字面意为“生的野蛮人”与“熟的野蛮人”）是外部强加的政治类别。相比之下，据伊能说，泰雅是一个族群自称。

en: In 1898, Inō launched a bulletin to publish research on Taiwan Indigenous Peoples. For the inaugural issue, he published a photomontage with representatives of eight tribes. The Atayal man in the montage was from the Wulai area, probably a member of the troop that visited Taipei in 1896. Due to technological constraints and the infrequent access Inō had to sitters, Inō’s montage was cobbled together out of black-and-white studio portraits and field photographs of uneven quality. This illustration could not capture the brilliant reds that were distributed to Atayal woman at Japanese outposts as the raw materials for the textiles that would in turn mesmerize Japanese souvenir hunters, ethnographers, and art fanciers. To remedy this problem, Inō commissioned a color painting as a substitute for display at the 1900 Paris Universal Exposition. While the photomontage displayed the Atayal man and woman in a simple vest and Chinese blouse, respectively, the painting took considerable artistic license to adorn them in ornate, bright-red traditional Atayal clothing.
zh: 1898年，伊能创办了一份公报，发表台湾原住民研究。创刊号上，他刊出了一幅八族代表的照片拼贴。拼贴中的泰雅男子来自乌来地区，大概是1896年访台北那批人中的一员。由于技术限制，加上伊能难得接触被摄者，他的拼贴是用质量参差的黑白照相馆肖像与田野照片拼凑而成的。这幅插图无法捕捉那些鲜艳的红色——日方在前哨分发给泰雅女子的是这些鲜红的织料，作为纺织品的原料，而这些纺织品反过来又迷住了日本寻购纪念品的人、民族志学者与艺术爱好者。为补救这一问题，伊能委托画家绘制了一幅彩色画，作为1900年巴黎万国博览会展出的替代品。照片拼贴中的泰雅男女分别穿着简单背心与中式上衣，画家则颇有自由发挥，画中的两人穿着华丽鲜红的泰雅传统服装。

en: It appears that Inō rarely left ethnological-survey encounters empty-handed. Inō Kanori’s large collection of cloths, carvings, and other implements formed the basis for the Taiwan National University Museum of Anthropology collection. The lion’s share of Inō’s over 430 specimens were obtained from his family in Iwate Prefecture by Utsurikawa Nenozo in the late 1920s, and they were the material foundation for the academic study of indigenous material culture in Taiwan at the PhD level.
zh: 看来伊能很少在民族学访查之后空手而归。伊能嘉矩大量的布料、雕刻与其他器具收藏，构成了国立台湾大学人类学博物馆藏品的基础。伊能430多件标本中的大部分是移川子之藏于1920年代末从伊能在岩手县的家人手中取得的，它们成为台湾原住民物质文化开展博士层次学术研究的实物基础。

en: Mori Ushinosuke returned to Inō’s site in late 1902 and early 1903 to photograph Watan Yūra and his family. Mori took multiple portraits of individuals and groups from Wulai and Rimogan (just upriver), with a focus on garments and cloth production especially. Five of these portraits were exhibited in nearly life-size reproductions for the five million visitors who attended the 1903 Osaka Industrial Exhibition. The Osaka posters were transported to the 1904 St. Louis World’s Fair and then picked up by American news services for further reproduction (see chapter 4). Besides the large impact the Osaka Expo had on the propagation of Inō’s map and taxonomy and Mori’s photographs, it also had a direct link to contemporary Taiwan. According to the National Taiwan Museum’s hundredth-anniversary guide, Mori
zh: 森丑之助于1902年末、1903年初回到伊能曾调查的地方，拍摄瓦丹有洛及其家人。森为乌来与利莫干（就在上游）的个人与群体拍了多幅肖像，尤其聚焦服装与布料生产。其中五幅以近真人大小的复制品展出，供参观1903年大阪工业博览会的五百万人观看。大阪海报被运往1904年圣路易斯世界博览会，随后又被美国新闻机构采用、进一步复制（见第4章）。大阪博览会除了对传播伊能的地图与分类、森的照片产生巨大影响外，还与当代台湾有直接联系。据国立台湾博物馆百周年指南，森

en: first came into contact with the exhibit of aboriginal culture at the [Osaka Industrial Exhibition] in 1903. Five years later, the Japanese government established the Affiliated Memorial Museum of the Business Property Bureau to commemorate the completion of Taiwan’s railroad network. Ranging from collecting objects for display, assortment of exhibit facilities, to the allotment of proper space, Mori had a hand in every aspect of exhibits. In 1915, the Taiwan Viceroy’s Office Museum... was finally completed and the specimens... were transferred to the new location. Mori transferred to the new museum and worked there until his retirement in 1924.
zh: “于1903年〔大阪工业博览会〕首次接触原住民文化展览。五年后，日本政府设立台湾总督府民政部殖产局附属博物馆，以纪念台湾铁路网竣工。从收集陈列物品、配置展览设施，到分配适当空间，森参与了展览的方方面面。1915年，台湾总督府博物馆……终于落成，标本……被迁往新址。森调往新博物馆，在那里工作直到1924年退休。”

en: To the extent that the TGG museum was the first stop for visitors and a school of colonialism for Japanese officials, Mori’s foundational work as the supplier, curator, and analyst of large collection of Atayal fabric in Taipei perhaps did more to associate “Atayals” with culture bearers than any of his myriad activities. On the photographic front, at the height of their popularity, Mori’s textile-rich Wulai photographs were reproduced in Japanese geography textbooks, commercial publications, and government reports, while Inō’s ethnic map found its way into the Japanese school curriculum.
zh: 就总督府博物馆既是访客的第一站、又是日本官员学习殖民治理的课堂而言，森在台北搜集、策展并研究大量泰雅织物所作的奠基工作，或许比他无数其他活动更有助于让人们把“泰雅人”视为其文化的承载者。在摄影方面，在其流行巅峰，森那些富含纺织品的乌来照片被复制进日本地理教科书、商业出版物与政府报告，而伊能的族群地图则进入了日本学校课程。

en: By 1915, the year Sakuma’s scorched-earth campaign terminated, any primary or high-school teacher in Japan had at hand the materials to demonstrate that Taiwan was inhabited by a number of ethnic groups, each in possession of its own customs, languages, and territories. With the installation of Mori’s collection at the Taipei museum, the same could be said of any important guest or ambitious official in Taiwan. This was a true accomplishment for the ethnologists. At this time, the overwhelming image of Taiwan Indigenous Peoples, even in textbooks but especially in newspapers, photo albums, and postcards, was of armed savage enemies of the state who would either soon go extinct or assimilate to Japanese culture.
zh: 到1915年，即佐久间焦土征伐结束那年，日本任何小学或中学教师手头都有材料，可以向学生展示台湾居住着若干族群，各有自己的习俗、语言与领土。随着森的收藏安置进台北博物馆，对台湾任何重要宾客或有抱负的官员，也可以这么说。这对民族学家是一项真正的成就。此时，台湾原住民的最占主导地位的形象——甚至在教科书中，尤其在报纸、相册与明信片中——是持械与国家为敌的“野蛮人”，他们要么很快灭绝，要么同化于日本文化。

en: ETHNIC TOURISM AND INDIGENOUS ART FORMS
zh: 族群观光与原住民艺术形式

en: As the frontier wars over camphor wound down in the 1910s, Atayal villages near Jiaobanshan and Wulai became regular stops for Japanese tourists and visiting dignitaries. The Atayal textiles that incorporated the red threads introduced in the treaty-port period could now be obtained at tourist-friendly trading posts as authentic indigenous cloth. During Japanese colonial rule, these garments made the transition from items of local consumption and everyday use to exported, high-quality handicrafts and art objects. In 1920, the protagonist of Satō Haruo’s novella
reported that the trading posts were stocking inferior knockoffs of the “genuine indigenous textiles” he sought,

while visiting Crown Prince Hirohito himself viewed an Atayal weaving demonstration in a Taiwan exhibition hall in 1923. The prince reportedly expressed admiration for their purity, color, and boldness of expression.

The indigenous trading posts and weaving demonstrations were also on the itineraries of Prince Chichibu in 1925 and Prince Asaka in 1927. A photo of the sword-bearing Asaka and his police escorts towering over three female Atayal weavers was splashed on the cover of the December 1927 issue of the
zh: 随着1910年代围绕樟脑的边疆战争渐息，角板山与乌来附近的泰雅村落成了日本游客与来访显贵的行程中经常停留的地方。那些用通商口岸时期引入的红线织成的泰雅纺织品，如今能在接待游客的贸易站买到，并被当作地道的原住民织物出售。日本殖民统治期间，这些服装从地方消费与日常使用的物品，转变为出口的高质量手工艺品与艺术品。1920年，佐藤春夫中篇小说《雾社》的主人公说，贸易站备办的是他寻求的“真正原住民纺织品”的劣质仿品，
而来访的裕仁皇太子本人于1923年在台湾一处展览馆观看了泰雅织布演示。据报道，皇太子对其纯正、色彩与表现的大胆表示赞赏。
原住民贸易站与织布演示也列入了秩父宫1925年、朝香宫1927年的行程。一张佩剑的朝香宫及其警察护卫高出三名泰雅女织工的照片，醒目刊登在《台湾时报》1927年12月号的封面上。

en: In 1933 the eminent scholar and critic Ozaki Hotsuma urged colonial officials to enforce Japan’s Important Arts Preservation Law in Taiwan so that traditional Atayal textiles, along with Paiwan woodcarvings, could be preserved as “national treasures.” Ozaki rued the extent to which indigenous culture had been degraded in Taiwan since its golden age. He believed that Atayalic artistic abilities had peaked in the distant past, when the world’s most archaic form of linear patterned cloth had emerged in the mountains of Taiwan. He argued that these artifacts, if preserved in a repository for scholarly and artistic appreciation, would reflect well on the empire itself. For Ozaki, the “normally administered areas” of Han residence possessed nothing of interest, except for derivative pieces imported from the continent.
zh: 1933年，著名学者兼评论家尾崎秀真敦促殖民官员在台湾执行日本《关于保存重要美术品等的法律》，以便把传统泰雅纺织品连同排湾木雕保存为“国宝”。尾崎为台湾原住民文化在他心目中的黄金时代过后衰落至此而惋惜。他相信，泰雅艺术能力在遥远过去已达顶峰，那时世界上最古老的线条纹样织物出现在台湾山地。他论证说，这些文物若保存在供学者研究、供艺术界鉴赏的典藏库中，将为帝国本身增光。对尾崎而言，汉人居住的“普通行政区”只有若干从大陆输入的仿制品值得一看。
body.review: 尾崎秀真的姓名见台北故宫博物院《故宫学术季刊》所载总督府博物馆活动；法名见日本文化厅公布的保存制度资料。

en: Like the Japanese aesthetes who praised the genius of Goryeo-era pottery while Japanese merchants undercut its production by flooding Korea with cheaper manufactured wares,

Ozaki did not connect the current “degraded state” of Atayal weaving to Japanese imports or other policies that eroded traditional forms of production. As early as 1900, the Government-General began to facilitate the construction of textile factories in Xindian. The local indigenous affairs field office recorded with satisfaction that Atayal women were being trained in Xindian and in Wulai to run the machines.

By 1938 journalist Harrison Forman, who shot numerous photographs at the same indigenous village visited by Princes Hirohito, Chichibu, and Asaka in the 1920s, observed that Atayal textiles had become luxury goods for local people. Traditional clothing required two weeks of labor to produce a single garment, wrote Forman, while secondhand Japanese clothing sold for about the price of two day’s labor on a road gang.
In a letter to the editor of

, Forman lamented that “the women too are dressed by the Japanese in cotton kimonos, which are symbolic of a movement that will rob another one of the few remaining native groups of the world of their own traditions and culture.”

Forman’s photograph, like a similar one by journalist Adachi Gen’ichirō taken in 1936, depicts Atayal women in Japanese clothing at work producing traditional garments for export, all while consciously posing for ethnic-tourism photographs (see
zh: 正如那些赞美高丽时代陶器的精湛技艺、而日本商人却用更便宜的机制器皿充斥朝鲜冲击了当地陶器生产的日本审美家一样，
尾崎没有把泰雅织布当前的“退化状态”与日本进口货或其他侵蚀传统生产形式的政策联系起来。早在1900年，总督府就开始促进新店纺织厂的建造。当地蕃务派驻机构满意地记录，泰雅女子正在新店与乌来受训操作机器。
到1938年，记者哈里森·福尔曼——他在1920年代裕仁、秩父宫、朝香宫等皇室成员到访过的同一个原住民村落拍了许多照片——观察到，泰雅纺织品已成为当地人的奢侈品。福尔曼写道，传统服装做一件需要两周工夫，而二手日本服装的售价约相当于在筑路队做两天工所得的工资。
在致《自然史》编辑的一封信中，福尔曼哀叹：“日本人也让女子们穿上了棉布和服，这象征着一场运动，它将剥夺世界上仅存的少数原住民族群之一的自身传统与文化。”

en: LEGACIES AND DILEMMAS
zh: 遗产与困境

en: Since the late 1980s, NGOs, the central government, and county offices have dispersed funding for indigenous language school curricula, the revival of dormant public rituals, and the manufacture of indigenous textiles, sculptures, and other items of material culture. As a result, the post-1990 affirmations of face-tattooing and head-taking, and the rediscovery of Atayal textiles and traditional music and dance, have erased much of the public and private stigma formerly attached to Atayal culture by Japanese and Han neighbors over the past century.
zh: 自1980年代末以来，非政府组织、中央政府与县政府拨付经费，用于学校里的原住民语言课程、一度中断的公共仪式的复兴，以及原住民纺织品、雕塑与其他物质文化物品的制造。结果，1990年后对纹面与猎首的肯定，以及对泰雅纺织品与传统音乐舞蹈的重新发现，消除了过去一个世纪日本与汉人邻居附着于泰雅文化的大部分流传于公共和私人生活中的污名。

en: The consultation of colonial-era ethnological writings, illustrations, and photographs has been a crucial component in many, if not all, of these revivalist projects.

The Japanese-period documentary record has been important for the authentication of native traditions in Taiwan. This recourse to materials preserved and stored by outsiders is testament to the transformative effects of the government-general’s relocation and assimilation policies, followed by decades of cultural oppression under the GMD. In a word, both the Japanese and the Taiwanese states have had a hand in deracinating Taiwan’s Austronesian populations. Perhaps more significantly, under GMD rule, 80–90 percent of Taiwan’s indigenes converted to Christianity, while roughly 50 percent migrated to urban environments antithetical to the maintenance of early twentieth-century markers of ethnic distinction.
zh: 查阅殖民时期的民族学著作、插图与照片，是许多这类复兴计划的重要环节。
日殖时期的文献记录，对台湾本土传统的认证一直很重要。这种借助外来者保存的资料的做法，证明了总督府迁移与同化政策的改造效应，以及随后国民党统治下数十年文化压迫的后果。一言以蔽之，日本殖民政权和战后的台湾政权，都使台湾南岛人群与原有的文化生活逐渐脱节。或许更重要的是，国民党统治下，80%—90%的台湾原住民皈依了基督教，约50%迁移到城市环境，在那里，二十世纪初用来区分族群的特征难以维持。

en: Recent ethnographic research suggests that top-down cultural politics are integral to the twenty-first-century indigenous renaissance in Taiwan. Anthropologist Michael Rudolph has noted that, as Christians, many indigenes did not initially identify with the revitalized symbolism, languages, and ceremonies that were being promoted by “elite traditionalists.” A period of time was required for adaptation and reappropriation. Scott Simon has written extensively about the emergence of an indigenous elite in the 1950s in response to GMD changes in property law and rural administration. These political operators often use identity politics to fulfill their own political ambitions and are sometimes viewed with derision by their rank-and-file constituents. Mitsuda Yayoi corroborates the general pattern: educated elites formulated and promoted particular versions of indigenous ethnic identity and subsequently mobilized followers to achieve state recognition for a given interpretation of tradition.

Hu Chia-yu has identified the same dynamic but tempers this view with the judgment that after a period of elite domination, the revitalization movement found a home in everyday life and rural indigenous villages. In the twenty-first century, she argues, “the enhancement of local cultures and indigenous identities are intertwined with the promotion of Taiwanese consciousness and identity...”
zh: 近期民族志研究表明，自上而下的文化政治是二十一世纪台湾原住民复兴不可或缺的部分。人类学家迈克尔·鲁道夫指出，作为基督徒，许多原住民起初并不认同“精英传统主义者”推广的重新启用的象征、语言与仪式。他们花了一段时间适应，并以自己的方式重新采用这些文化实践。斯科特·西蒙大量著述，论及1950年代原住民精英为回应国民党财产法与乡村行政变革而出现。这些政治操盘手常常利用身份政治实现自身政治野心，有时被本族普通选民轻视。满田弥生印证了这一总体模式：受教育精英制定并推广特定版本的原住民族群身份，随后动员追随者，使国家对传统的某一特定诠释予以承认。
胡家瑜也指出了这一过程，但她补充说：经过一段精英主导之后，复兴运动进入原住民村落的日常生活。她论证说，在二十一世纪，“地方文化与原住民身份的提升，与台湾意识及身份的推广交织在一起……”

en: Can indigenous renaissance in Taiwan, therefore, be likened to top-down cultural revitalization projects in other postcolonial situations? Critical scholarship of the Indian case has suggested that unifying symbols of Indian, Hindu, or Maharashtra continuity, cohesion, and distinctiveness have been invoked by cultural elites to quash internal dissent in the name of national survival.

In Taiwan, on a much smaller scale, energized groups of activists have won official recognition for their ethnic groups to become eligible for office holding, public funding, and political patronage that accrue with the state’s imprimatur. Since 2001 the number of recognized indigenous groups in Taiwan has climbed from nine to sixteen.

While the motives of such leaders and their followers are mixed and complicated, these battles have occurred in an institutional framework that incentivizes the homogenization of particular ethnic identities and the accentuation of differences among them.
And it was precisely these two processes that Inō Kanori and Mori Ushinosuke sought to consolidate as collectors, exhibitors, editors, and writers in the early twentieth century.
zh: 那么，台湾的原住民复兴能否比作其他后殖民情境中自上而下的文化振兴工程？对印度案例的批判学术表明，文化精英援引象征印度、印度教或马哈拉施特拉延续、团结和独特性的标志，以民族生存之名压制内部异议。
在台湾，以小得多的规模，充满活力的活动家群体已为其族群赢得官方承认，从而获得担任公职、公共资金与随国家认可而来的政治扶持的资格。自2001年以来，台湾获承认的原住民族群数量已从九攀升到十六。
虽然这类领袖及其追随者的动机复杂混杂，这些斗争却发生在一个促使各族群内部认同趋于一致、族群之间差别进一步凸显的制度框架中。
而正是这两个过程，伊能嘉矩与森丑之助在二十世纪初作为收藏家、展览者、编辑与作者力求巩固。

en: Some would consider it irresponsible to put the Taiwan indigenous renaissance on a par with postcolonial Indian nationalism. The move to historicize putatively timeless entities such as the Atayal can undermine indigenous claims to an autonomous political identity, according to this line of thought.

James Clifford’s classic study of the courtroom travails of the Mashpee Indians, whose legal claims to rights and resources hinged on their ability to document the autochthony and continuity of their community by recourse to visible markers of culture, is a case in point.

To suggest that any indigenous identity has been staged, as I have done in this chapter, can be considered an attack upon the claims to collective redress that are part and parcel of indigenous rights recovery movements.
zh: 有些人会认为，把台湾原住民复兴与后殖民印度民族主义等量齐观是不负责任的。按这一思路，把泰雅这类据称永恒的实体历史化，会削弱原住民对自主政治身份的申索。
詹姆斯·克利福德对马什皮印第安人诉讼经历的经典研究就是恰当例证：他们对权利与资源的法律申索，取决于能否诉诸文化的可见标记，证明其共同体的本土起源和历史延续。
指出某个原住民族群的身份通过展演呈现——如我在本章所做——可能被视为对集体补偿申索的攻击，而这种申索是原住民权利恢复运动不可或缺的部分。

en: However, not all proponents of preservationism are indigenes laboring against staggering odds to regain stolen rights or establish a modicum of dignity. In post–martial law Taiwan, Han intellectuals who have invoked indigenous “otherness” as a tool for revitalizing Taiwanese national culture or for pulling Taiwan out of China’s cultural orbit are primarily interested in Taiwan Indigenous Peoples as symbols. The symbolism of authentic, timeless, and non-Han indigenous peoples secures Taiwan’s Austronesian heritage in this discourse.

The problem here is that the preservationist ethos encoded in essentialist definitions of ethnic belonging can backfire by creating unreasonable expectations that have grave real-world consequences. The notion that indigenous peoples are inauthentic or not truly indigenous if they do not wear traditional clothing or bear other markers of ethnic difference easily recognized by outsiders is, in fact, a common one. This fixation on authenticity shades into the political view that visibly assimilated indigenous peoples should ipso facto lose rights or privileges (such as access to waterways and hunting grounds or preferential treatment on university-entrance or civil-service exams).
The specter of the inauthentic (and undeserving) indigenous person is never far from the surface.
zh: 然而，并非所有主张保存传统的人都是在惊人逆境中奋力夺回被窃权利、或争得起码的尊严的原住民。在解严后的台湾，那些援引原住民“他者性”作为振兴台湾民族文化、或把台湾拉出中国文化轨道工具的汉人知识分子，看重的主要是台湾原住民的象征价值。在这套话语中，“真实”、超越历史、区别于汉人的原住民形象，支撑着台湾的南岛文化传承这一说法。
这里的问题在于，把族群归属视为由固定本质决定的这种文化保存观，可能因制造不合理期待而适得其反，带来严重的现实后果。认为原住民若不穿传统服装、或不带有外来者易识别的其他族群差异标记就不正宗、并非真正原住民，这种观念实际上很常见。对正宗性的执着渐变为一种政治看法：明显同化的原住民因此应失去权利或特权（如使用水域和猎场，或大学入学、公务员考试的优待）。
人们随时可能被怀疑是“不真实”的原住民，因而被认为不配享有这些权利。

en: As was the case in the period of Japanese colonial rule, there are scholars today who find certain elements of indigenous cultures intrinsically valuable and of high aesthetic worth. Han anthropologists have worked in recent years to reinstate reconstructed forms of indigenous dance and song into the fabric of everyday life by promoting public performance as education. One critic of this movement has asked:
zh: 正如日本殖民统治时期的情形，今日也有学者发现原住民文化的某些要素本身有价值，也具有高度的审美价值。汉人人类学家近年努力通过把公开演出用作教育手段，使重构后的原住民歌舞重新融入日常生活。这一运动的一位批评者问道：

en: Shall those young [indigenes] who have been in contact with Han society for a long time identify with an image... that has stagnated for several decades or centuries? Or shall they identify with a culture that has —as a result of inevitable historical development—interacted with other ethnic groups? And what kind of “Aborigines” shall non-Aborigines identify with? Is it possible that [Han preservationists]—in order to redress the Han’s former hegemony or for reasons of political correctness—unconsciously bring all possibility for the Aborigines’ pluralist cultural development to an end?
zh: 那些长期接触汉人社会的年轻〔原住民〕，应当认同一个……数十年乃至数百年未变的形象吗？还是应当认同一种随着历史发展而不可避免地与其他族群发生互动的文化？而非原住民又该认同怎样的“原住民”形象？有没有可能，〔主张保存传统的汉人〕——为纠正汉人昔日的霸权，或出于政治正确的原因——不自觉地终结了原住民多元文化发展的一切可能？

en: In this view, the interests of curators, ethnologists, neoprimitivists, and progressive Han activists are pitted against the majority of indigenes who have lived among the Han for many decades and who do not wish to turn back the clock. This proposition assumes that visible markers of identity, which perhaps define indigenes to outsiders, somehow exhaust self-conceptions of belonging from an emic perspective. Hu Chia-yu’s study of Saisiyat memory, identity, and ritual life controverts such a view. She indicates that indigenous ethnic identities in Taiwan are also maintained through oral transmissions that interact in complex ways with material artifacts. Hu writes:
zh: 按这一看法，策展人、民族学家、新原始主义者与进步汉人活动家的利益，与大多数原住民对立——后者已与汉人同住数十年，不愿回到从前。这一命题假设，外人或许凭身份的可见标志来辨认原住民，却把这些标志当成了原住民自己理解群体归属的全部依据。胡家瑜对赛夏记忆、身份与仪式生活的研究反驳了这种看法。她表明，台湾的原住民族群身份也通过口头传承维系，后者与实物以复杂方式互动。胡写道：

en: …non-verbal expressions are heavily emphasized [in] Saisiyat ritual practices. However, the persuasiveness of ritual materials is combined with elaborated multi-sensory operations. The process of practicing rituals, touching sacred objects, tasting ancestral foods and drinks, listening to ritual speeches or songs, and making body movements are all perceived as major sources of sensory multiplicity. The senses as embodied powers are mediated through the material properties of sacred objects, ritual foods, or stylized bodily actions. Thus... the ancestral past is continuously sensed, recognized and articulated in the present to build and secure permanence in the Saisiyat community.
zh: ……赛夏的仪式非常重视非言语表达。然而，仪式材料的说服力与精心组织、调动多种感官的活动相结合。践行仪式、触摸圣物、品尝祖先传下的饮食、聆听仪式演说或歌谣、做出身体动作的过程，都被视为多重感官体验的主要来源。感官是作用于身体的能力，通过圣物、仪式食物的物质特性或程式化的身体动作来发挥作用。因此……祖先的过去在当下被持续感知、识别与表述，由此建立并维系赛夏共同体的延续。

en: In other words, the meanings of these objects for those who treasure them as mnemonic sites cannot be divined by mere visual inspection or abstract contemplation. They derive their identity-making efficacy through use in specific contexts that are largely unavailable to outsiders.
zh: 换言之，这些物件对珍视它们、视之为记忆之所的人的意义，无法单靠观看或抽象思考来理解。它们通过在特定情境中的使用获得身份建构的效力，而外来者大多无缘参与这些场合。

en: The three Meiji-era collectors who did so much to preserve, categorize, and enliven these objects for outsiders, Inō Kanori, Mori Ushinosuke, and Torii Ryūzō, could scarcely have imagined, I think, that Saisiyat, Atayal, Bunun, and other indigenous groups would still be around in the twenty-first century to utilize their collections. If their taxonomic labors and collecting proclivities have furthered indigenous renewal and persistence, as it seems they have to some extent, this long-term consequence was unintended, although not contrary to the spirit of their work in its own context.
zh: 我想，那三位为外来者保存、分类并让外界看到这些物件的鲜活之处的明治时期收藏家——伊能嘉矩、森丑之助与鸟居龙藏——几乎无法想象，赛夏、泰雅、布农及其他原住民族群在二十一世纪仍会存在，并利用他们的收藏。如果他们的分类工作与收藏热忱促进了原住民的更新与存续（看来在某种程度上确实如此），这一长期成果并不在他们的预料之中，却仍与他们在当时开展这些工作的用意相合。
